From the root tij in the sense of 'to sharpen', with the suffix ina, the change of j to kh, and the change to ṇ, [resulting in] tikhiṇaṃ. From tij itself, with the suffix va, and the change of j to b, [resulting in] tibbaṃ. Three [terms] for 'fierce'. From the root caṇḍ in the sense of 'anger', [resulting in] caṇḍaṃ. From the root ujj in the sense of 'strength' and 'protection', with the suffix a, and the change of jj to gg, [resulting in] uggaṃ. From the root khar in the sense of 'destruction', with the suffix a, [resulting in] kharaṃ.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0465] jaṅgame. Gamu gamane, dvittādi, jaṅgamaṃ. Cara gamane, a, caraṃ. Tasati calatīti tasaṃ, tasa ubbege, ubbego bhayaṃ, calanañca. Carabhismā caro, majjhe dīgho, carācaraṃ, abbhāsante vā rāgamo, carācaraṃ, sabbatra apaccayo. Iṅgampi, iṅgatīti iṅgo, iṅga gamane.

Four [terms] for 'moving'. From the root gam in the sense of 'to go', with doubling etc., [resulting in] jaṅgamaṃ. From the root car in the sense of 'to go', with the suffix a, [resulting in] caraṃ. 'It trembles and moves', thus tasaṃ; from the root tas in the sense of 'agitation', and agitation means fear and also movement. From the root car, with lengthening in the middle, it becomes carācaraṃ; or at the end of the reduplication, there is the augment ra, resulting in carācaraṃ; in all cases with the suffix a. Also iṅgaṃ; 'it moves', thus iṅgaṃ; from the root iṅg in the sense of 'to go'.

712-713. Dvayaṃ calanamatte. Kampa calane. Cala kampane, sabbatra kattari yu.

712-713. Two [terms] for 'mere movement'. From the root kamp in the sense of 'to shake'. From the root cal in the sense of 'to tremble'; in both cases, with the suffix yu in the agentive sense.

Dvayaṃ adhike. Atiriccatīti atiritto, rica viyojanasampaṭicchanagatīsu, to, bhujādi. Adhi eti gacchatīti adhiko, i gamane, ko.

Two [terms] for 'excessive'. 'It is in excess', thus atiritto; from the root ric in the sense of 'separation', 'acceptance', and 'going', with the suffix ta, as in the bhujādi group. 'It goes beyond', thus adhiko; from the root i in the sense of 'to go', with the suffix ka.

Jaṅgamā pāṇito añño thāvaro nāma, tiṭṭhatīti thāvaro, ṭhā gatinivattiyaṃ, varo, vaṇṇavikāro, thāvaro, ṭhāvaropītyeke.

Other than moving living beings, there is what is called thāvaro (immovable). 'It stands', thus thāvaro; from the root ṭhā in the sense of 'cessation of movement', with the suffix vara and a change of letter, [resulting in] thāvaro. Some say it is also ṭhāvara.

Catukkaṃ lole. Lola ummādane. Cala kampane, dvittādi, cañcalaṃ. Tara plavanataraṇesu, taraṃ lātīti taralaṃ, ete calanamattepi.

Four [terms] for 'restless'. From the root lul in the sense of 'agitation'. From the root cal in the sense of 'to tremble', with doubling etc., [resulting in] cañcalaṃ. From the root tar in the sense of 'floating' and 'crossing'; 'it takes on trembling', thus taralaṃ. These terms also refer to mere movement.

Catukkaṃ purāṇe. Pure bhavo purāṇo, yadādinā napaccayo, ṇattaṃ. Purā bhavo purātano, tanapaccayo. Sanaṃsaddo [M 0.0466] iha sattamyanto purāṇatthe nipāto. Tatra bhavo sanantano, pubbe viya sanaṃsaddo vā, tatrāpi pubbe viya niggahītāgamo. Ciraṃsaddo nipāto sattamyanto purāṇattho iha gayhate, tatra bhavo cirantano. Niggahītalopo cirakālādīsu.

Four [terms] for 'ancient'. 'Existing formerly' is purāṇo; by the rule for yadādi, the suffix is ṇa, with the change to ṇ. 'Existing long ago' is purātano; the suffix is tana. Here the word sana, a particle ending in the seventh case, is in the sense of 'ancient'. That which exists therein is sanantano; or, as before, the word is sanaṃ, and there too, as before, is the niggahīta augment. The word ciraṃ, a particle ending in the seventh case, is here taken in the sense of 'ancient'; that which exists therein is cirantano. The elision of the niggahīta occurs in words such as cirakāla.

Catukkaṃ abhinave. Patito aggo yassa paccaggho, gassa gho, bahuko vā aggho yassa paccaggho, anekatthattā hi upasagganipātānaṃ bahukattho ettha patisaddo. Navasaddāsakatthe tano, navassa nubhāvo ca. Navo eva abhinavo, nu thutiyaṃ, a, navo.

Four [terms] for 'new'. 'That whose front has just arrived' is paccaggho, with g becoming gh; or, 'that which has much value' is paccaggho, for since prefixes and particles have many meanings, here the word pati has the meaning of 'much'. From the word nava, in its own sense, with the suffix tana, and the change of nava to nū, [resulting in nūtana]. Navo itself is abhinavo. From the root nu in the sense of 'praise', with the suffix a, [resulting in] navo.

714-715. Pañcakaṃ kakkhaḷe. Kantatīti kurūraṃ, ūro, kantassa ca kurādeso, kara hiṃsāyaṃ vā, ūro, assu. Kaṭha kicchajīvane, muddhajadutiyanto dhātu, ino, vaṇṇavipariyaye kathinantipi. Dala vidāraṇe, ho, ḷattaṃ, baha vuddhimhi vā, bassa do, ḷanto ca, daḷhaṃ daha bhasmīkaraṇe vā, a, ḷanto ca. Niṭṭhātīti niṭṭhuraṃ, ṭhā gatinivattiyaṃ, uro. Kakkha hasane, alo, ḷattaṃ. Kaṭhoraṃ, jaraṭhaṃ, muttimaṃ, muttampi, kaṭha kicchajīvane, oro. Jara jīraṇe, bhūvādi, ṭho. Mutti kathinyaṃ, taṃyogā muttimaṃ. Apaccaye muttaṃ.

714-715. Five [terms] for 'harsh'. 'It cuts', thus kurūraṃ; from the root kant, with the suffix ūra, and the substitution of kura for kant; or from the root kar in the sense of 'harming', with the suffix ūra, and the change of a to u. From the root kaṭh in the sense of 'difficult living'—a root ending in the second retroflex consonant—with the suffix ina; by metathesis, it is also kaṭhina. From the root dal in the sense of 'splitting', with the suffix ha and the change to ḷ, [resulting in] daḷhaṃ; or from the root bah in the sense of 'growth', with b becoming d and ending in ḷ, [resulting in] daḷhaṃ; or from the root dah in the sense of 'burning', with the suffix a and ending in ḷ. 'It stands firm', thus niṭṭhuraṃ; from the root ṭhā in the sense of 'cessation of movement', with the suffix ura. From the root kakkh in the sense of 'laughing', with the suffix ala and the change to ḷ. Also kaṭhoraṃ, jaraṭhaṃ, muttimaṃ, and muttaṃ. From the root kaṭh in the sense of 'difficult living', with the suffix ora, [comes kaṭhoraṃ]. From the root jar in the sense of 'decaying', of the bhūvādi group, with the suffix ṭha, [comes jaraṭhaṃ]. Mutti means 'hardness'; from its connection, muttimaṃ. The form is muttaṃ without a suffix.

Sattakaṃ ante. Ama gamane, to, anto, anitthī. Paripubbo pariyanto. Papubbo panto. Pacchā bhavo pacchimo. Ante bhavo antimo, imo. Jaghane sādhu jighaññaṃ, yo, assi. Caratismā imo. Carimaṃ, carasaddā vā imo.

Seven [terms] for 'end'. From the root am in the sense of 'to go', with the suffix ta, [resulting in] anto, which is not feminine. With the prefix pari, it becomes pariyanto. With the prefix pa, it becomes panto. 'Existing behind' is pacchimo. 'Existing at the end' is antimo, with the suffix ima. 'Good in the hind part' is jighaññaṃ, with the suffix ya and the change of a to i. From carati, with the suffix ima, it becomes carimaṃ; or from the word cara, with the suffix ima.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0467] paṭhame. Pubba pūraṇe, a. Aggaṃ seṭṭhepi vuttaṃ. Paṭha viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, amo, patha saṅkhyāne vā, amo, vaṇṇavikāro, paṭhamaṃ, pathamantipi. Ādīyate paṭhamaṃ gaṇhīyateti ādi, i, pume, sosaddo ādissa pulliṅgattajotako, purimaṃ, puratthāpi, bhavatthe imatthā.

Four [terms] for 'first'. From the root pubb in the sense of 'to fill', with the suffix a. Aggaṃ has also been stated in the sense of 'best'. From the root paṭh in the sense of 'distinct speech', with the suffix ama; or from the root path in the sense of 'enumeration', with the suffix ama and a change of letter, [resulting in] paṭhamaṃ, also pathama. 'It is taken first', thus ādi; from the root i, in the masculine gender; the word so indicates the masculine gender of ādi. Also purimaṃ and puratthā; in the sense of 'being', with the suffixes ima and tthā.

Dvayaṃ anucchavike. Paṭiggahito rūpo patirūpo. Chaviyā anurūpaṃ anucchavikaṃ, sakatthe ko.

Two [terms] for 'suitable'. An accepted form is patirūpo. That which is suitable for one's appearance is anucchavikaṃ; with the suffix ka in its own sense.

Dvayaṃ niratthake. Mūha vecitte, a, hassa gho. Natthi attho yassa, sakatthe ko.

Two [terms] for 'meaningless'. From the root muh in the sense of 'bewilderment', with the suffix a, and h becoming gh, [resulting in mogha]. That which has no meaning, with the suffix ka in its own sense, [is anatthaka].

716. Dvayaṃ pākaṭe. Visiṭṭho attā yassa byattaṃ. Puṭa pakāsane, puṭa vikāsane vā.

716. Two [terms] for 'manifest'. That whose nature is distinct is byattaṃ. From the root puṭ in the sense of 'making clear', or puṭ in the sense of 'developing'.

Tikaṃ mudumhi. Muda modane, u, muda saṃsagge vā. Sobhanaṃ kumāraṃ kanti yassa. Ku sadde, alo, manto ca.

Three [terms] for 'soft'. From the root mud in the sense of 'delighting', with the suffix u; or mud in the sense of 'association'. That which has the beautiful charm of a boy is komalaṃ. From the root ku in the sense of 'sound', with the suffix ala, and also manta.

Dvayaṃ indriyaggayhe. Akkhaṃ indriyaṃ patigataṃ nissitaṃ, akkhena vā patigataṃ paccakkhaṃ, kate samāse patisaddassa pubbanipāto abhidhānato. Indriyaṃ cakkhādikaṃ, tena gayhaṃ indriyaggayhaṃ.

Two [terms] for 'perceptible by the senses'. Akkhaṃ is a sense faculty; that which has gone to or is dependent on it, or that which is perceived through the sense faculty, is paccakkhaṃ. When the compound is formed, the word pati is placed first by convention. A sense faculty, such as the eye, etc.; that which is to be grasped by it is indriyaggayhaṃ.

Dvayaṃ apaccakkhe. Paccakkhaviparītaṃ apaccakkhaṃ, paramāṇvādi. Indriyaṃ atikkantaṃ atindriyaṃ.

Two [terms] for 'imperceptible'. The opposite of paccakkha is apaccakkhaṃ, such as atoms, etc. That which transcends the senses is atindriyaṃ.

717. Catukkaṃ aññatthe. Itarasaddo pāṭipadiko aññatthavācako, idaṃsaddā vā taro aññatthe, daṃlopo ca[M 0.0468]. Aññasaddā sakatthe taro. Eko seṭṭhepi vutto. Aññasaddo pāṭipadiko bhinnattho, na ñāyateti vā añño.

717. Four [terms] for 'other'. The word itara is a nominal stem expressing the meaning 'other'; or, from the word idaṃ, with the suffix tara in the sense of 'other', and elision of daṃ. From the word añña, with the suffix tara in its own sense. Eko is also stated in the sense of 'best'. The word añña is a nominal stem with a different meaning; or, 'that which is not known' is añño.

Tikaṃ nānappakāre. Bahavo vidhā pakārā assa bahuvidho. Vicittā vidhā yassa vividho.

Three [terms] for 'diverse'. That which has many kinds or varieties is bahuvidho. That which has varied kinds is vividho.

Dvayaṃ anivārite. Natthi bādho nisedho yassa abādhaṃ. Natthi aggaḷaṃ assa.

Two [terms] for 'unhindered'. That which has no hindrance or prohibition is abādhaṃ. That which has no impediment is anaggaḷaṃ.

718. Catukkaṃ asahāye. Asahāyatthe ekato ākī, cco, ko ca, ekākī, ekacco. Aññatthepi ekako vutto. Samā tulyatthā.

718. Four [terms] for 'solitary'. In the sense of 'without a companion', from eka, with the suffixes ākī, cca, and ka, [resulting in] ekākī and ekacco. Ekako is also stated in another sense. Samā has the meaning of 'equal'.

Anekasambandhini sādhāraṇādidvayaṃ. Saha ādhāraṇena vattatīti sādhāraṇaṃ, yadādi, thiyaṃ sādhāraṇī, sādhāraṇā ca. Samānameva sāmaññaṃ, yo, sāmaññā itthiyaṃ.

Two [terms], sādhāraṇa and so on, in the sense of 'related to many'. 'It exists with a common basis', thus sādhāraṇaṃ; by the rule for yadādi; in the feminine, sādhāraṇī and sādhāraṇā. 'Sameness itself' is sāmaññaṃ, with the suffix ya; sāmaññā in the feminine.

Dvayaṃ appāvakāse. Sambādhate asmiṃ, ro. Saṃsaddā kaṭo, yadādi, saṅkaṭaṃ, saha āvaraṇena vattatīti vā saṅkaṭaṃ, sahattho saṃsaddo.

Two [terms] for 'confined space'. 'One is constrained in this', thus sambādhaṃ, with the suffix ra. From the word saṃ, with kaṭa, by the rule for yadādi, [it becomes] saṅkaṭaṃ; or, 'it exists with an obstruction', thus saṅkaṭaṃ; the word saṃ has the meaning of 'with'.

719. Vāmaṃ kaḷevaraṃ vāmakāyo sabyaṃ nāma. “Sabyaṃ vāme ca dakkhiṇe”ti cintāmaṇiṭīkā 21.84 hi ajayo, sava gatiyaṃ, yo. Dakkhiṇaṃ kaḷevaraṃ apasabyaṃ, sabyato apagataṃ apasabyaṃ.

719. The left body, the left side, is called sabyaṃ. For Ajaya says: 'Sabyaṃ is on the left and on the right'; from the root sava in the sense of 'to go', with the suffix ya. The right body is apasabyaṃ; 'that which has gone away from the left' is apasabyaṃ.

Dvayaṃ [M 0.0469] viparīte. Paṭikūlati āvaratīti paṭikūlaṃ, kūla āvaraṇe. Apasabyaṃ dakkhiṇepi vuttaṃ.

Two terms for 'reversed'. That which is adverse and obstructs is paṭikūlaṃ; from the root kūla in the sense of 'obstructing'. Apasabyaṃ is also stated in the sense of 'right'.

Duradhigamanto pathaṃ gahanaṃ, yathā – gahanametaṃ satthaṃ, dubbivekamiccattho. Gacchantaṃ hantīti gahanaṃ, gahaṇampi, yadādi. Kala gamane, ilo, kaliṃ lātīti vā kalilaṃ.

A path whose end is difficult to reach is gahanaṃ (a thicket); for example, 'this teaching is gahanaṃ', meaning 'difficult to discern'. That which strikes those who go is gahanaṃ; also gahaṇaṃ. From the root kala in the sense of 'going', with the suffix ilo; or, that which takes up strife (kali) is kalilaṃ.

720-721. Dvayaṃ bahuppakāre. Uccañca taṃ avacañceti uccāvacaṃ, kammadhārayo. Bahavo bhedā assa.

720-721. Two terms for 'manifold'. That which is both high and low is uccāvacaṃ; it is a kammadhāraya compound. That which has many distinctions.

Tikaṃ janādinirantaragate. Saṅka saṅkāyaṃ, to. Kira pakkhepavikkhipanesu, to, iṇṇādeso. Saṅka saṅkāyaṃ, ulo, saṅkulaṃ, saṃpubbo kula santāne vā, ro.

Three terms for 'crowded' or 'dense'. From the root saṅka in the sense of 'being crowded', with the suffix to. From the root kira in the sense of 'throwing' and 'scattering', with the suffix to, and the substitution of iṇṇa. From the root saṅka in the sense of 'being crowded', with the suffix ulo, resulting in saṅkulaṃ; or from the root kula in the sense of 'continuity' with the prefix saṃ, with the suffix ro.

Siloko cheke. Kato abhyāsito hattho padattho yena katahattho. Kusa silesane, alo. Pakaṭṭhā vīṇā assa. Abhijānāti abhiñño. Sikkha vijjopādāne, to. Puṇa kammani subhe, ro. Paṭa gamane, u. Chidi dvidhākaraṇe, kattari a, dassa ko. Cata yācane, uro. Dala dittiyaṃ, kho, lassa ko, dakkha vuḍḍhiyaṃ vā, a, dakkha vuḍḍhihiṃsāgatisīghesu vā. Pisa hiṃsābaladānaniketanesu, alo, pesalo. Katamukho, katīpi, katasaddo [M 0.0470] abhyāsitattho, kataṃ abyāsitaṃ mukhaṃ upāyo anenāti katamukho. Kataṃ assatthīti katī.

A group of synonyms for 'skillful'. One by whom the hand is made practiced and ready is katahattho. From the root kusa in the sense of 'joining', with the suffix alo. One who has an excellent lute is paviṇo. One who knows thoroughly is abhiñño. From the root sikkha in the sense of 'acquiring knowledge', with the suffix to. From the root puṇa in the sense of 'good action', with the suffix ro. From the root paṭa in the sense of 'going', with the suffix u. From the root chidi in the sense of 'dividing in two', with the suffix a in the agentive sense, and d becoming k. From the root cata in the sense of 'requesting', with the suffix uro. From the root dala in the sense of 'shining', with the suffix kho, and l becoming k; or from the root dakkha in the sense of 'growth', with the suffix a; or dakkha in the senses of 'growth', 'harming', 'going', and 'speed'. From the root pisa in the senses of 'harming', 'strength', 'giving', and 'abode', with the suffix alo, resulting in pesalo. Katamukho, and also katī; the word kata means 'practiced'; one by whom the means is practiced is katamukho. One who has practice is katī.

Sattakaṃ bāle. Bala pāṇane, balatīti bālo, assāsitapassāsitamattena jīvati, na paññājīvitenātyattho. Dā kucchāyaṃ gatiyaṃ vā, tu, dvittaṃ, rassādi. Jala dhaññe, a, ḷattaṃ. Mūha vecitte, lo, vaṇṇavipariyayo, mūḷho. Manda jaḷatte. Bālyayogā bāliso, iso. Añño, yathājātopi, na jānātīti añño. Yādiso jāto viveko yathājāto.

Seven terms for a fool. From the root bala in the sense of 'to breathe'; one is called bālo because one breathes, living merely by inhaling and exhaling, not by the life of wisdom—this is the meaning. From the root dā in the sense of 'contempt' or 'going', with the suffix tu, doubling, shortening, etc. From the root jala in the sense of 'being stiff', with the suffix a, and the substitution of ḷa. From the root mūha in the sense of 'bewilderment', with the suffix lo, and transposition of letters, thus mūḷho. From the root manda in the sense of 'dullness'. Through connection with foolishness, bāliso, with the suffix iso. Añño: because one does not know, one is añño. Yathājāto: as one is born, so is one's discernment.

722. Tikaṃ bhāgyasampanne. Puññaṃ, sukatañca yasmiṃ atthi puññavā, sukatī, vantu, ī ca. Dhanaṃ gahaṇaṃ laddhoti dhañño, yo. Dvayaṃ mahāvīriye. Mahādhiti mahāvīriyo. Dvayaṃ mahicche. Mahāsayopi.

722. Three terms for the fortunate. One in whom there is merit and good deeds is puññavā and sukatī, with the suffixes vantu and ī respectively. One who has obtained wealth is dhañño, with the suffix yo. Two terms for one of great energy: mahādhiti and mahāvīriyo. Two terms for one of great desire: also mahāsayo.

Dvayaṃ bahulahadaye, pasatthahadaye ca. Hadayaṃ bahulaṃ, pasatthañca yassa hadayī, hadayālu ca, tabbahule ī, ālu ca, suhadayopi.

Two terms for one with an abundant heart and one with a praised heart. One whose heart is abundant and praised is hadayī and hadayālu, with the suffixes ī and ālu in the sense of abundance. Also suhadayo.

723. Dvayaṃ haṭṭhacitte. “Hāsamano vikubbāno, pamāno haṭṭhamānaso”ti amara 21.7 amarasīho. Dvayaṃ dummane. Duṭṭhaṃ, dukkhitaṃ vā mano yassa. Virūpaṃ mano yassa. Antamanopi.

723. Two terms for one with a joyful mind. "Hāsamano, vikubbāno, pamāno, haṭṭhamānaso," says Amarasīha. Two terms for one with a sorrowful mind. One whose mind is corrupted or afflicted. One whose mind is distorted. Also antamano.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0471] bahuppade. Yācakānaṃ vadaṃ vacanaṃ jānātīti vadāniyo, vadaññū ca, iyo, rū ca, pubbatraññassa nādeso, majjhadīgho ca. Dāne soṇḍo pasuto. Soṇḍasaddotra majjamadetyeke, thūlalakkhopyatra, dānatthaṃ thūlaṃ lakkhaṃ assa.

Four terms for one who gives much. One who knows the speech of beggars is vadāniyo and vadaññū, with the suffixes iyo and rū respectively; in the former, there is a substitution of ṇa for ñña, and a lengthening of the middle vowel. One who is devoted and intent on giving. Some say the word soṇḍa here means 'intoxicated'. Here it also means 'having a prominent characteristic'; one's prominent characteristic is for the sake of giving.

724. Siloko pākaṭamatte. Khyā pakāsane, to. Patipubbo i gamane, to. Abhimukhaṃ etīti patīto. Ñā avabodhane, to, paññāto, abhiññāto ca. Patha khyāne. Su gatibuddhīsu, to, suto, vissuto ca, su savane vā, kamme to. Vida ñāṇe, vidito. Sidhu saṃrādhe, to, sidha saṃsiddhiyaṃ vā. Kaṭa gatiyaṃ, dassanaṃ kaṭatīti pākaṭo, upasaggassa dīgho.

724. A group of synonyms in the sense of 'evident' or 'well-known'. From the root khyā in the sense of 'to reveal', with the suffix to. From the root i in the sense of 'to go', with the prefix pati, with the suffix to; one who comes face to face is patīto. From the root ñā in the sense of 'to understand', with the suffix to, thus paññāto and abhiññāto. From the root patha in the sense of 'to proclaim'. From the root su in the senses of 'going' or 'understanding', with the suffix to, thus suto and vissuto; or from the root su in the sense of 'hearing', with the suffix to in the passive sense. From the root vida in the sense of 'knowledge', thus vidito. From the root sidhu in the sense of 'accomplishment', with the suffix to; or from sidha in the sense of 'perfection'. From the root kaṭa in the sense of 'movement'; it goes towards sight, thus pākaṭo; the prefix is lengthened.

725. Tipādaṃ issare. Īsa issariye, īsatīti issaro, aro, rassādi, dvittaṃ. Nī naye, ṇvu, nāyako. Saṃ dhanaṃ assatthīti sāmī, dīghādi, rassante sāmipi. Pā rakkhaṇe,ti, rassādi, pati. Adhipubbe adhipati. Īsa issariye, a, īso. Pabhavatīti pabhu, u, pabhūpi. Aya gamane, yo, ayyo. Adhipātīti adhipo, ro. Adhibhavatīti adhibhū, kvi. Nī naye, ritu, netā.

725. A group of terms for a ruler. From the root īsa in the sense of 'lordship'; one who rules is issaro, with the suffix aro, shortening, and doubling. From the root nī in the sense of 'to lead', with the suffix ṇvu, hence nāyako. One who has wealth is sāmī, with lengthening, and sāmipi with shortening at the end. From the root pā in the sense of 'to protect', with the suffix ti and shortening, thus pati. With adhi as a prefix, adhipati. From the root īsa in the sense of 'lordship', with the suffix a, hence īso. One who has great power is pabhu, with the suffix u, also pabhū. From the root aya in the sense of 'to go', with the suffix yo, thus ayyo. One who rules over is adhipo, with the suffix ro. One who overpowers is adhibhū, with the suffix kvi. From the root nī in the sense of 'to lead', with the suffix ritu, thus netā.

Tikaṃ [M 0.0472] bahudhane. Ibhaṃ arahatīti ibbho, vo, vaṇṇavipariyayo. Jhe cintāyaṃ, a, ajjhāyati dhanaṃ aḍḍho, jhassa ḍho, asarūpadvittaṃ, rassādi ca. Dhanā atisaye ī, dhanī.

Three terms for the wealthy. One who is worthy of an elephant (ibha) is ibbho, with the suffix vo and transposition of letters. From the root jhe in the sense of 'thought', with the suffix a; one who thinks about wealth is aḍḍho, with jh becoming ḍh, dissimilar doubling, and shortening. From dhana in the sense of abundance, with the suffix ī, thus dhanī.

726. Dvayaṃ dakkhiṇeyye. Dānaṃ paṭiggaṇhituṃ arahatīti dānāraho, dakkha vuddhiyaṃ, sīghatthe ca, dakkhanti bhogasampadādīhi yāya, sā dakkhiṇā, iṇo, taṃ arahatīti dakkhiṇeyyo.

726. Two terms for one worthy of offerings. One who is worthy to receive gifts is dānāraho. From the root dakkha in the sense of 'increase' and also 'swiftness'; that by which they increase through wealth and prosperity is dakkhiṇā, with the suffix iṇa. One who is worthy of that is dakkhiṇeyyo.

Dvayaṃ snehavati. Siniha pītiyaṃ, dho, hassa do, siniddho, vaccho sineho yassatthi vacchalo, lo.

Two terms for the affectionate. From the root siniha in the sense of 'affection', with the suffix dho, and ha becoming da, thus siniddho. One who has affection like for a calf (vaccha) is vacchalo, with the suffix lo.

Pamāṇiko parikkhako, parikkhate avadhārayate pamāṇehi atthanti parikkhako, ikkha dassanaṅkesu, ṇvu. Kāraṇaṃ jānātīti kāraṇiko, iko.

Pamāṇiko is an examiner (parikkhako); one who examines and determines the meaning by means of measures is a parikkhako. From the root ikkha in the sense of 'seeing' and 'marking', with the suffix ṇvu. One who knows the cause is kāraṇiko, with the suffix iko.

Dvayaṃ āsatte. Sanja saṅge, to. Taṃ taṃ vatthu paraṃ padhānaṃ assa tapparo.

Two terms for the attached. From the root sanja in the sense of 'attachment', with the suffix to. One for whom that particular thing is the supreme and foremost endeavor is tapparo.

727. Tikaṃ kāruṇike. Karuṇā sīlaṃ assa kāruṇiko. Dayā karuṇā yassatthi dayālu, ālu. Dukkhitesu suṭṭhu ramatīti sūrato, upasaggassa dīghatā.

727. Three terms for the compassionate. One whose nature is compassion is kāruṇiko. One who has pity and compassion is dayālu, with the suffix ālu. One who delights well in the afflicted is sūrato; the prefix is lengthened.

Iṭṭhatthe [M 0.0473] abhimatappayojane uyyuto puggalo ussuko nāma, uṭṭhānaṃ suṭṭhu kāyatīti ussuko, hasādyanuṭṭheyaṃ.

A person intent on a desired purpose, on an agreeable aim, is called ussuko. One who undertakes exertion well is ussuko. This should not be undertaken with laughter and so forth.

Yo ālasyāvasādīhi anutiṭṭhati, so dīghasutto, dīghañca taṃ suttañca, tamiva caratīti dīghasuttaṃ, dīghasuttapariyantikaṃ kāriyaṃ karotīti dīghasutto. Cirena kriyānuṭṭhānaṃ assa.

One who persists in laziness and dejection is a dīghasutto (procrastinator). It is a long thread (dīghaṃ suttaṃ), and one acts like that, thus dīghasuttaṃ. One who performs tasks that are at the end of a long thread is a dīghasutto. One's performance of actions is delayed.

728. Dvayaṃ parāyatte, parasmiṃ, parena vā adhīno parādhīno, ajhantā sakatthe ino yadādinā. Paratanto, paravā, attavāpi nāthavā (amara 21.26, tantayatīti tanto, tanta kuṭumbadhāraṇe, a, paro tanto niyāmako yassa. Paro seṭṭho nāyako, attā ca atthīti paravā, attavā ca, vantu.

728. Two terms for one dependent on another. One who is subordinate to another or by another is parādhīno; the suffix ino is in the sense of 'self' according to the ajhantā group, etc. Paratanto, paravā, and also attavā. That which sustains is tanto, from the root tanta in the sense of 'sustaining a household', with the suffix a; one whose regulator is another is paratanto. One who has another as a superior leader, and also oneself, is paravā and attavā, with the suffix vantu.

Āyattatāmatte catukkaṃ. Yata payatane, āpubbo avasībhāve, to. Antena samīpena sahāti santako, sakatthe ko. Pariggayhate “saka”nti karīyateti pariggaho. Adhigato ino pabhū yenāti adhīno.

Four terms in the sense of 'dependence'. From the root yata in the sense of 'effort', with the prefix ā in the sense of 'non-mastery', with the suffix to. That which is with the end or with nearness is santako; the suffix ko is in the sense of 'self'. It is taken as 'one's own', thus pariggaho. One by whom a lord or master is attained is adhīno.

Sena attanā īritaṃ sīlaṃ assāti serī, tasmiṃ serini ca sacchando vattati, sassa attano chando yassatthīti sacchando, a. Savaso, sayaṃvasī, niravaggahopi.

One whose conduct is impelled by oneself is serī. In that independent one, one's own will prevails. One who has one's own will is sacchando, with the suffix a. Also savaso, sayaṃvasī, and niravaggaho.

729. Guṇadose [M 0.0474] anisamma anupaparikkhitvā yo karoti, so jammo, jama adane, mo.

729. Whoever acts without considering, without investigating virtues and faults, is a jammo. From the root jama in the sense of 'eating', with the suffix mo.

Dvayaṃ atitaṇhe. Lubha lobhe, a, dvittaṃ, bhassa po, lolupo, lolubhopi.

Two terms for one with excessive craving. From the root lubha in the sense of 'greed', with the suffix a, reduplication, and bha becoming pa, thus lolupo, and also lolubho.

Tikaṃ luddhe. Gidha abhikaṅkhāyaṃ, to. Lubha giddhiyaṃ, to. Lola ummādane, a, lolo. Atha mahātaṇhātitaṇhagiddhānaṃ ko bhedo? Mahātaṇho nānārammaṇaṃ icchati, atitaṇho ekasmimpi ārammaṇe anekavāraṃ, adhikañca tasati, giddho pana ubhayathāpīti ayametesaṃ viseso.

Three terms for the greedy. From the root gidha in the sense of 'desire', with the suffix to. From the root lubha in the sense of 'craving', with the suffix to. From the root lola in the sense of 'agitation', with the suffix a, thus lolo. Now, what is the difference between one with great craving (mahātaṇho), one with excessive craving (atitaṇho), and one who is greedy (giddho)? One with great craving desires various objects; one with excessive craving repeatedly and excessively thirsts for even a single object. One who is greedy, however, does both—this is the distinction among them.

Yo kriyāsu mando, so kuṇṭho, kuṇṭha paṭighāte, ālasye ca, a.

One who is slow in actions is kuṇṭho. From the root kuṇṭha in the sense of 'hindrance' and 'laziness', with the suffix a.

730. Pañcakaṃ kāmake. Kamu icchāyaṃ, curādi, ritu, kāmayitā, kāritalope kamitā. Yumhi kāmano, kamanopi. Ṇīpaccaye kāmī, ṇukapaccaye kāmuko, anuko, abhikopyatra, anukāmayate anuko, kvi. Abhikāmayate abhiko, kvi. Atikopi.

730. Five terms for one who desires. From the root kamu in the sense of 'desire', of the curādi class, with the suffix ritu, thus kāmayitā; with the elision of the causative affix, kamitā. Also kāmano and kamano. With the suffix ṇī, kāmī; with the suffix ṇuka, kāmuko. Also anuko and abhiko are in this context. One who covets is anuko, with the suffix kvi. One who intensely desires is abhiko, with the suffix kvi. Also atiko.

Dvayaṃ matte. Suṇḍā surā, tatra kusalo soṇḍo, pānāgāraṃ vā suṇḍā, tatra bhavo, ṭhitaṃ vā soṇḍo. Mada ummāde[M 0.0475], to. Ukkaṭo, khivopi, madena uddhato ukkaṭo, yadādinā uto kaṭo mattatthe pāṇini 5.2.29. Khiva made, a.

Two terms for the intoxicated. 'Suṇḍā' is liquor; one skilled therein is 'soṇḍo'. Alternatively, 'suṇḍā' is a tavern; one who is present or established there is 'soṇḍo'. The root 'mada' is in the sense of intoxication; the suffix is 'ta'. Also 'ukkaṭo' and 'khivo'. One who is arrogant from intoxication is 'ukkaṭo'. By a rule of the 'yadādi' group, 'uta' becomes 'kaṭa' in the sense of 'intoxicated'. The root 'khiva' is in the sense of intoxication; the suffix is 'a'.

Tikaṃ vacanakārini. Pavattinivattīsu vidhātuṃ sakyo vidheyyo, iyyo. Ādesitaṃ, ādarena vā suṇotīti assavo, rassādi, a. Sundaraṃ vaco ācariyādīnaṃ etasmiṃ hetubhūteti subbaco. Vinayaggāhīpi, vinayaṃ vidhipaṭisedhavacanaṃ gahetuṃ sīlo vinayaggāhī.

Three terms for the obedient. One who can be instructed in what should be done and what should be avoided is 'vidheyyo'; the suffix is 'iyya'. One who listens to instruction, or listens with respect, is 'assavo'; there is shortening of the vowel, etc., and the suffix is 'a'. One for whom the good word of teachers and so forth is the cause is 'subbaco'. Also 'vinayaggāhī'; one whose nature it is to grasp the Vinaya—the words of prescription and prohibition—is 'vinayaggāhī'.

731. Taṅkhaṇuppattiñāṇaṃ paṭibhā, tāya yutto pagabbho, sīghameva gabbhatīti pagabbho, gabbha dhāraṇe.

731. The knowledge of immediate arising is 'paṭibhā'; one endowed with that is 'pagabbho'. One who quickly conceives is 'pagabbho'; the root 'gabbha' is in the sense of conceiving.

Tikaṃ bhīruke. Bhī bhayaṃ sīlo yassa bhīsīlo. Bhāyatīti bhīru, bhī bhaye, ru. Rukapaccaye bhīruko, sakatthe vā ko.

Three terms for the fearful. One whose nature is fear is 'bhīsīlo'. One who fears is 'bhīru'; from the root 'bhī' in the sense of fear, with the suffix 'ru'. With the suffix 'ruka', the form is 'bhīruko'; alternatively, 'ka' is a pleonastic suffix.

Dvayaṃ asūre. Na vīro sūro avīro. Kucchitatarattā kātaro, kussa kādeso.

Two terms for the cowardly. One who is not a hero, not brave, is 'avīro'. Because of being more contemptible, one is 'kātaro'; 'ku' is substituted by 'kā'.

Dvayaṃ hiṃsāsīle, hananasīlo hiṃsāsīlo, ghātuko, uko, hanassa ghāto. Sarāru, hiṃsopi.

Two terms for one of a harmful nature. One whose nature is to kill is 'hiṃsāsīlo'. Also 'ghātuko'; the suffix is 'uka', and 'han' becomes 'ghāta'. Also 'sarāru' and 'hiṃso'.

732. Tikaṃ kodhayutte. Kudha kope, kujjhanasīlo kodhano, yu. Dusa dose, dosano, paṭigho[M 0.0476], yu. Kupa kope, kupatīti kopī, ṇī. Amarisanopi, natthi marisanaṃ khamā assa amarisano, marisa asahane.

732. Three terms for one endowed with anger. The root 'kudha' is in the sense of anger; one whose nature it is to be angry is 'kodhano'; the suffix is 'yu'. The root 'dusa' is in the sense of hatred; from this come 'dosano' and 'paṭigho'; the suffix is 'yu'. The root 'kupa' is in the sense of anger; one who is angry is 'kopī'; the suffix is 'ṇī'. Also 'amarisano'; one who has no forgiveness ('marisanaṃ', i.e., 'khamā') is 'amarisano'; the root 'marisa' is in the sense of not enduring.

Dvayaṃ adhikakodhayutte. Caṇḍateti caṇḍo, a, caṇḍa kope. Atirekaṃ kujjhatīti accantakodhano. Accantakopanopi, tadā kupato yu.

Two terms for one with excessive anger. One who is fierce is 'caṇḍo'; the suffix is 'a'; the root 'caṇḍa' is in the sense of anger. One who is exceedingly angry is 'accantakodhano'. Also 'accantakopano'; this is formed from the root 'kupa' with the suffix 'yu'.

Pañcakaṃ khantiyutte. Saha khamane, yu. Khamu sahane, yu. Tumhi khantā, satthādi. Titikkhā yassatthīti titikkhavā. Mantumhi khantimā, savibhattissa ntussa ā.

Five terms for one endowed with patience. The root 'saha' is in the sense of enduring; the suffix is 'yu'. The root 'khamu' is in the sense of enduring; the suffix is 'yu'. With the suffix 'tu', the form is 'khantā', like 'satthā' and so forth. One who possesses endurance ('titikkhā') is 'titikkhavā'. With the suffix 'mantu', the form is 'khantimā'; the suffix 'ntu' along with its case ending becomes 'ā'.

733. Dvayaṃ saddhāyutte. Hi padapūraṇe. Saddhā yassatthīti saddhālu. Saddhā ratanattayādīsu pasādo, taṇhā, ādaro ca. Dvayaṃ dhajayutte. Cihane ca paṭākāyaṃ, dhajo sophe ca soṇḍike, sopho pulliṅgaṃ.

733. Two terms for one endowed with faith. 'Hi' is a particle for filling out the line. One who has faith ('saddhā') is 'saddhālu'. Faith is confidence in the Triple Gem and so forth, and also delight, craving, and respect. Two terms for one endowed with a banner. 'Dhaja' means a sign and a flag; 'dhaja' also means swelling and an elephant's trunk. 'Sopha' is masculine.

Dvayaṃ niddāsīle. Niddā eva sīlaṃ yassa so niddāsīlo. Dvayaṃ pabhāyutte. Bhā dittimhi, sarapaccayo, rassādi, dvittañca, bhassaro, bhāsā rati yassāti vā bhassaro, rassādi eva. Sassa dvittābhāve bhāsuro, assu, bhāsa dittiyaṃ vā, uro, atha vā dvayaṃ bahukathāyutte, bhāsāsu sabbāsu bahūsu kathāsu ramatīti bhassaro, kvi, bhāsatīti vā bhassaro, aro, rassādi, dvittañca, bhāsāsu ramatīti vā bhāsaro, kvi, majjharasso, bhāsatīti vā bhāsaro, aro, imasmiṃ pakkhe assuttābhāvo.

Two terms for one of a sleepy nature. One whose nature is sleep itself is 'niddāsīlo'. Two terms for one endowed with radiance. From the root 'bhā' in the sense of radiance, with the suffix 'sara', shortening of the vowel, etc., and doubling, comes 'bhassaro'. Alternatively, one whose delight is in radiance ('bhāsā') is 'bhassaro', with shortening, etc., as before. In the absence of the doubling of 's', the form is 'bhāsuro'; the suffix is 'assu'. Or, from the root 'bhāsa' in the sense of radiance, with the suffix 'ura'. Alternatively, two terms for one who talks much. One who delights in all kinds of much talk is 'bhassaro'; the suffix is 'kvi'. Or, one who speaks is 'bhassaro'; the suffix is 'ara', with shortening, etc., and doubling. Or, one who delights in speech is 'bhāsaro'; the suffix is 'kvi', with shortening of the middle vowel. Or, one who speaks is 'bhāsaro'; the suffix is 'ara'; in this alternative, there is no 'assu'.

734. Tikaṃ [M 0.0477] nagge. Na gacchatīti naggo, dvittaṃ, lagga saṅge vā, nattaṃ, naji laji bile vā, ṇo, jassa go, dvittaṃ. Disā eva ambaraṃ vatthaṃ etassa, na pakativatthanti digambaro. Sassa go. Natthi vatthaṃ etassa, atha vā digambarā vatthā, aññatitthiko avattho cāti ete dve naggo nāma, naggā nāmāti vā, “te itthikhyā po, satta pakaraṇāni abhidhammo nāmā”tyādīsu viya saññāsaññīsaddānaṃ vacanabhedassāpi sambhavato. Naggo ca naggo ca naggā, purimasmiṃ pakkhe pana sāmaññatāya ekavacananiddeso.

734. Three terms for the naked. One who does not go is 'naggo'; there is doubling. Or, from 'lagga' in the sense of attachment, with 'l' becoming 'n'. Or, from the roots 'naji' or 'laji' in the sense of shame, with the suffix 'ṇa', 'j' becoming 'g', and doubling. One whose garment is the directions themselves, not an ordinary garment, is 'digambaro'. The 's' of 'disā' becomes 'g'. One who has no garment is 'avattho'. Alternatively, the 'digambara' and the 'avattho'—these two are called 'naggo', or 'naggā' (plural). This is because a difference in number between the name and the named is possible, as in examples like 'the seven treatises are called the Abhidhamma'. 'Naggo' and 'naggo' make 'naggā'; however, in the first case, the singular is used to denote the general category.

Dvayaṃ bhakkhake. Ghasa adane, maro, ghasmaro. Bhakkha adane, ṇvu.

Two terms for an eater. From the root 'ghasa' in the sense of eating, with the suffix 'mara', comes 'ghasmaro'. From the root 'bhakkha' in the sense of eating, with the suffix 'ṇvu', comes 'bhakkhaka'.

Vattuṃ sotuñca akusalo, vacane savane ca akusalo eḷamūgo nāma, eḷo badhiro, mūgo avacano, kammadhārayo, saṭhepi eḷamūgo.

One who is unskilled in speaking and hearing, that is, unskilled in speech and listening, is called 'eḷamūgo'. 'Eḷo' means deaf, 'mūgo' means speechless; it is a karmadhāraya compound. 'Eḷamūgo' is also used for a cheat.

735. Mukharādayo tayo appiyavādini. Vājhāvājhesu mukhaṃ assatthi, nindāyaṃ ro. Ninditaṃ mukhaṃ yassa dummukho. Abaddhaṃ anaggaḷaṃ mukhaṃ yassa abaddhamukho.

735. The three terms beginning with 'mukhara' are for one who speaks unpleasantly. One who has a mouth for disputes is 'mukhara'; the suffix 'ra' is in the sense of censure. One whose mouth is contemptible is 'dummukho'. One whose mouth is unrestrained and unbolted is 'abaddhamukho'.

Bahu [M 0.0478] ca gārayhañca vaco yassa so vācālo nāma. Kucchitā vācā assa santīti vācālo, nindāyaṃ lo.

One whose speech is both abundant and reprehensible is called 'vācālo'. Alternatively, one whose speech is contemptible is 'vācālo'; the suffix 'la' is in the sense of censure.

Dvayaṃ suvacane. Vadatīti vattā, pasaṃsāyaṃ tu. Vadatīti vado. So padapūraṇe.

Two terms for one who speaks well. One who speaks is 'vattā'; the suffix 'tu' is in the sense of praise. One who speaks is 'vado'. The word 'so' is a particle for filling out a line of verse.

736. Tikaṃ attaniye. Netabboti niyo, niyo eva nijo, nī naye, ṇyo, yassa jo, samīpe jāyatīti vā nijo. Sassa attano ayaṃ sako, idamatthe ko, so eva vā sako, sassāyaṃ sako, ṇo. Attani jāto attaniyo, aniyo.

736. Three terms for one's own. 'Niyo' means 'to be led'; 'niyo' itself becomes 'nijo', from the root 'nī' (to lead) with the suffix 'ṇya', where 'y' becomes 'j'. Alternatively, 'nijo' means that which is born nearby. From 'sa' (one's own), this is 'sako'; the suffix 'ka' is in the sense of 'this'. Or, 'sa' itself is 'sako'. Or, from 'sa', this is 'sako' with the suffix 'ṇa'. Born in oneself is 'attaniyo'; the suffix is 'aniya'.

Tikaṃ acchariye. Vipubbo maha pūjāyaṃ, bhūvādi, ṇyo, mantalopo, vimhayo. Āpubbo cara gatibhakkhanesu, a, carassa cchariyo, rassādi ca, acchariyo. Na bhavitthāti abbhuto, asarūpadvittaṃ, rasso ca, abhūtopi saddanītipadamālāyaṃ 340.1 piṭṭhesu passitabbaṃ.

Three terms for a marvel. From the root 'maha' (to honor) of the 'bhūvādi' group, with the prefix 'vi-', the suffix 'ṇya', and elision of the final part, comes 'vimhayo'. From the root 'cara' (to move, to eat), with the prefix 'ā-', the suffix 'a', the change of 'car' to 'cchariya', and shortening of the vowel, etc., comes 'acchariyo'. 'Abbhuto' means 'not having been'; there is non-identical doubling and shortening of the vowel. Also 'abhūto'.

Sokādīhi itikattabbatāpaṭipattisuñño vihattho, byākulo ca. Vikkhitto hattho yassa vihattho. Kula saṅkhyāne viāpubbo.

One who is devoid of the practice of what should be done due to sorrow and so forth is 'vihattho', and also 'byākulo'. One whose hands are scattered is 'vihattho'. From the root 'kula' in the sense of counting, with the prefixes 'vi-' and 'ā-', comes 'byākulo'.

Katasannāho vadhudyato hantumudyato uyyuto ātatāyī nāma. “Vadhuyyutto”tipi pāṭho. Āpubbo tā pālane, ṇī, dvittaṃ, ākārantānamāyo, ātatāyī.

One who is armed, intent on killing, intent on striking, and prepared for violence is called an 'ātatāyī'. There is also the reading 'vadhuyyutto'. From the root 'tā' in the sense of protecting, with the prefix 'ā-', the suffix 'ṇī', and doubling; for roots ending in 'ā', 'āya' is the augment, thus 'ātatāyī'.

737. Sīsacchejjamhi [M 0.0479] sīsacchedārahe vajjho. Hantabboti vajjho, hana hiṃsāyaṃ, ṇyo, hanassa vadho, jhassa jho. Asarūpadvittaṃ, vajjho.

737. In the context of beheading, one who is deserving of beheading is 'vajjho'. 'Vajjho' means one who should be killed; from the root 'han' in the sense of injuring, with the suffix 'ṇya', 'han' becomes 'vadha', and 'jh' becomes 'jho'. It is a non-identical doubling, 'vajjho'.

Tikaṃ vakkāsaye. Nikantatīti nikato, kanta chedane, a, nalopo. Saṭha ketave, a. Natthi ujutā yassa anuju.

Three terms for the deceitful. One who cuts down is 'nikato'; from the root 'kanta' in the sense of cutting, with the suffix 'a' and elision of 'n'. From the root 'saṭha' in the sense of cheating, with the suffix 'a', comes 'saṭho'. One who has no uprightness is 'anuju'.

Tikaṃ bhedakārake. Sūca pesuññe, ṇvu. Pisi sañcuṇṇane, pisi avayave vā, pisatīti pisuṇo, yadādinā uno, ṇattaṃ. Kaṇṇe japatīti, aluttasamāso, arucitabbarocakepi kaṇṇejapo.

Three terms for one who causes division. From the root 'sūca' in the sense of slander, with the suffix 'ṇvu', comes 'sūcaka'. From the root 'pisi' in the sense of grinding, or 'pisi' in the sense of a part; one who grinds is 'pisuṇo'; by a rule of the 'yadādi' group, the suffix is 'una', and 'n' becomes 'ṇ'. One who whispers in the ear is 'kaṇṇejapo'; it is an unelided compound. 'Kaṇṇejapo' is also one who speaks what is disagreeable or agreeable.

Dvayaṃ paharaṇasīle. Dhubbī hiṃsāyaṃ, to, bhujādi. Vañcayate vippalapateti vañcako, vañca gamane.

Two terms for one who is prone to striking. From the root 'dhubbī' of the 'bhujādi' group, in the sense of harming, with the suffix 'ta', comes 'dhutto'. One who deceives or prevaricates is 'vañcako'; from the root 'vañca' in the sense of going.

738. Ariyāsāmaññena ca bālapurisassa lakkhaṇamāha. Hi padapūraṇe. Yo puriso yo jano, janapariyāyo cettha purisasaddo “dve mahāpurisā abhinikkhantā”tyādīsu viya, anisamma anupaparikkhitvā vadhabandhanādikiccaṃ karoti, so khalu ekantato “capalo”ti viññeyyo, kasmā? Avinicchitakārittā sammā avinicchitassa kāriyassa karaṇasīlattā. Capa kakkaraṇe, capa santāne vā, alo, capalo.

738. He states the characteristic of a foolish person in both noble and common usage. 'Hi' is a particle for filling out the line. That person, that individual—here the word 'purisa' is a synonym for 'jana', as in 'two great persons have gone forth' and so forth—who, without reflecting or investigating, performs actions such as killing and binding, is indeed to be understood as 'capalo' (rash). Why? Because of acting without proper consideration, that is, being in the habit of doing a deed that has not been properly decided upon. From the root 'capa' in the sense of shaking, or 'capa' in the sense of continuing, with the suffix 'ala', comes 'capalo'.

739. Catukkaṃ [M 0.0480] kadariye. Kucchitaṃ dadātīti khuddo, do, kassa kho, adānasīlatāya samparāyesu khuddaṃ bubhukkhissāmīti vā khuddo, khuda bubhukkhāyaṃ, do anāgatatthe. Parānupabhogena atthasañcayasīlattā kucchito ariyo atthapati kadariyo, adāyakattā kucchitaṃ ṭhānaṃ aratīti vā kadariyo, iyo. Dānādīsu namanābhāvena thaddhena maccherayuttacittena sahitatāya thaddhamaccharī, ī. Kucchito paṇo yassa kapaṇo, kipacāno, mitappacopi. Kucchitaṃ pacānoti dutiyāsamāso. Mitaṃ pacatīti mitappaco, ṇo.

739. Four terms for the miserly. One who gives wretchedly is 'khuddo'; the suffix is 'da'. Or, from 'kassa kho' (to whom?), because of the habit of not giving. Or, thinking 'I will be hungry in future lives', one is 'khuddo'; from the root 'khuda' (to be hungry), with the suffix 'da' in the future sense. Because of the habit of accumulating wealth for the non-enjoyment of others, a contemptible master is a 'kadariyo'. Or, because of not giving, one goes to a contemptible state, thus 'kadariyo'; the suffix is 'iya'. Due to being rigid, lacking inclination for giving and so forth, and being endowed with a mind possessed of stinginess, one is a 'thaddhamaccharī'; the suffix is 'ī'. One whose wealth is contemptible is 'kapaṇo'; also 'kipacāno' and 'mitappaco'. 'Kucchitaṃ pacāno' (cooking wretchedly) is an accusative compound. One who cooks moderately is 'mitappaco'; the suffix is 'ṇa'.

Addhaṃ dalidde. Natthi kiñcanaṃ appamattakampi dhanaṃ yassa akiñcano. Dalidda duggatiyaṃ, a, dala vidāraṇe vā, ido, dvittaṃ. Dīna duggatabhāve, dīno, di khaye vā, īno. Natthi dhanaṃ assa. Ninditaṃ gamanaṃ assa duggato.

A term for the poor. One who has nothing, not even a little wealth, is 'akiñcano'. 'Dalidda' is in the sense of misfortune, with the suffix 'a'; or from the root 'dala', to split, with the suffix 'ido' and doubling. 'Dīna' is in the sense of a state of suffering, becoming 'dīno'; or from the root 'di', to perish, with the suffix 'īno'. He has no wealth. One whose going is despised is 'duggato'.

740. Yaṃ kammaṃ “idamahaṃ uppādessāmī”ti asambhāvitaṃ acintitameva hutvā sampattaṃ, taṃ “kākatālīya”ntyuccate. Tālassa idaṃ phalaṃ tālaṃ, kāko ca tālañca kākatālāni, tehi sadisaṃ kammaṃ kākatāliyaṃ, kākassa, tālaphalassa uḍḍanapatanasadisaṃ kammantyattho.

740. An action that occurs unexpectedly, without having been thought of or intended with the thought, 'I will produce this,' is called 'kākatālīya'. The fruit of the palm tree is 'tāla'; a crow and a palm fruit are 'kākatālāni'. An action similar to these is 'kākatāliyaṃ', meaning an action similar to the flying of a crow and the falling of a palm fruit.

Catukkaṃ yācake. Yācanaṃ karotīti yācanako, yācatīti vā, yāca yācane, yu. Sakatthe ko. Attha yācanāyaṃ, atthanaṃ attho, so assatthīti atthī. Ṇvu, yācako[M 0.0481]. “Mādisassa dhanaṃ datvā rājā saggaṃ gamissatī”tyādinā dānaphalaṃ vaṇṇetvā vakati yācatīti vanibbako, vaṇṇassa vani, vaka ādāne, ādānamettha yācanameva.

Four terms for 'beggar'. One who performs begging is 'yācanako', or one who begs; from the root 'yāca', to beg, with the suffix 'yu'. The suffix 'ko' is used in its own sense. From the root 'attha', to request: 'atthanaṃ' means a request; one who has that is 'atthī'. With the suffix 'ṇvu' comes 'yācako'. One who, by praising the fruit of giving with words such as, 'By giving wealth to one like me, the king will go to heaven,' speaks and begs, is 'vanibbako'; 'vaṇṇa' becomes 'vani', from the root 'vaka', to take, where taking here is simply begging.

741. Kiñcidūnakantaṃ patipādena nāmaṃ. Pakkhisappamacchādayo aṇḍato jātattā aṇḍajā. Narādayo pana gabbhāsayasaṅkhātajalābuto, tatra vā jātattā jalābujā. Kimi ca ḍaṃsā ca ādinā makasamaṅgurādayo ca sedajā, sedakāraṇattā usmā sedo, tato jātā sedajā. Devo ca ādinā brahmanerayikādayo ca opapātikā, upagantvā patatīti upapātī, ṇī, soḷasavassuddesikādiko attabhāvo, so yesamatthi, te opapātikā.

741. A name given by way of a slight deficiency. Birds, snakes, fish, and so forth, are 'aṇḍajā' (egg-born) because they are born from eggs. Humans and so forth, however, are 'jalābujā' (womb-born) because they are born from the womb, which is called 'jalābu', or are born therein. Worms, gadflies, and so forth, including mosquitoes and eels, are 'sedajā' (moisture-born); heat is the cause of moisture, and those born from that are 'sedajā'. Gods and so forth, including Brahmas and hell-beings, are 'opapātikā' (spontaneously born); 'upapātī' means one who appears spontaneously, with the suffix 'ṇī'; this refers to an individual existence like one appearing at sixteen years of age; those who have that existence are 'opapātikā'.

742. Jaṇṇumatte jaṇṇuppamāṇayutte udakādimhi jaṇṇutaggho, jaṇṇuppamāṇo jaṇṇutaggho, pamāṇatthe taggho, jaṇṇuppamāṇo jaṇṇumatto, pamāṇatthe matto moggallāne 4.47 sutte passitabbaṃ, tasmiṃ.

742. In the sense of 'knee-deep': 'jaṇṇutaggho' means having the measure of a knee in water and so forth. 'Jaṇṇuppamāṇo' is 'jaṇṇutaggho'; the suffix 'taggho' is in the sense of measure. 'Jaṇṇuppamāṇo' is also 'jaṇṇumatto'; the suffix 'matto' is in the sense of measure, in that context.

Kiñcidūnake appamattakayutte kappo pāṇini 5.4.67, ūnassa appakatāya kappīyati ekādivasena paricchijjatīti kappo, kappa paricchedane.

In the sense of 'slightly deficient' or 'connected with a small measure', the term is 'kappo'. Because of the smallness of the deficiency, it is limited or defined by a day and so forth, thus 'kappo'; from the root 'kappa', to limit or define.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0482] pariyāpanne. Anto gacchatīti antaggataṃ, “lopañca tatrākāro”ti olope aāgamo, dvittaṃ. Antogatampi. Paricchinditvā āpannaṃ gahitaṃ pariyāpannaṃ. Gādha patiṭṭhāyaṃ, anto ogādhatīti antogadhaṃ, rasso, ogādhatīti ogadhaṃ.

Four terms for 'included' or 'comprised'. That which goes within is 'antaggataṃ'; by the rule 'lopañca tatrākāro', there is insertion of 'ā' in elision, and doubling. Also 'antogataṃ'. That which is grasped after being delimited is 'pariyāpannaṃ'. From the root 'gādha', to be established; that which plunges within is 'antogadhaṃ'; with shortening, 'ogādhati' becomes 'ogadhaṃ'.

743. Dvayaṃ sādhite. Rādha sādha siddhiyaṃ, kammani to.

743. Two terms for 'accomplished' or 'achieved'. From the roots 'rādha' and 'sādha', in the sense of accomplishment, with the suffix 'ta' in the passive sense.

Dvayaṃ kuthite. Paca pāke, atīte kattari to, tassa kko, calopo. Kutha nippakke, to.

Two terms for 'cooked' or 'boiled'. From the root 'paca', to cook, with the suffix 'ta' in the past active voice; its 't' becomes 'kka', and 'c' is elided (e.g., pakko). From the root 'kutha', to be thoroughly cooked, with the suffix 'ta'.

Āpadaṃ byasanaṃ patto āpanno nāma, atipīḷanaṃ āpajjatīti āpanno, “ā tukodhamudāṭṭīsū”ti hi ekakkharakoso ekakkharakosa 14 gāthā . Pada gamane, “āpanno ca vipattimhi, patte ca vāccaliṅgiko”ti nānatthasaṅgaho.

One who has reached calamity or misfortune is called 'āpanno'; one who encounters excessive oppression is 'āpanno'. Indeed, this is from the Ekakkharakosa: 'ā tukodhamudāṭṭīsū'. From the root 'pada', to go. From the Nānatthasaṅgaha: '“āpanno” is used in the sense of calamity, and in the sense of having attained; it is an adjective.'

Dvayaṃ paresamavasagate. Natthi vaso āyatto paresaṃ etasmiṃ serībhūteti vivaso, avaso ca.

Two terms for being under the control of others. One who is not self-controlled but dependent on others is 'vivaso', and also 'avaso'.

744. Chakkaṃ khitte. Nuda peraṇe, nuda khepe vā, to, tassa inno. Aninnādese bhujādi, nutto. Nutopi. Asu khepane, to, bhujādi, atto. Khipa peraṇe, to.

744. Six terms for 'thrown' or 'cast'. From 'nuda', to impel, or 'nuda', to scatter, with the suffix 'ta', which becomes 'inna' (e.g., nunno). In the absence of the 'inna' substitution, from the bhujādi group, it is 'nutto'. Also 'nutto'. From 'asu', to throw, with the suffix 'ta', from the bhujādi group, it is 'atto'. From 'khipa', to impel, with the suffix 'ta'.

Īra [M 0.0483] gatiyaṃ, kampane ca, ito, īrito. Āpubbo vidha peraṇe, to, āviddho.

From the root 'īra', to move and to shake, with the suffix 'ita', comes 'īrito'. From the root 'vidha', to impel, with the prefix 'ā-', with the suffix 'ta', comes 'āviddho'.

Catukkaṃ kampite. Kampa calane, dhū vidhunane, kampane ca. Dhūto, ādhūto, cala kampane, calito. Vellito, pekhitopi. Vella calanattho. Pekha gatyattho, pekhito.

Four terms for 'shaken' or 'trembling'. From 'kampa', to move; from 'dhū', to shake and to tremble, come 'dhūto' and 'ādhūto'; from 'cala', to tremble, comes 'calito'. Also 'vellito' and 'pekhito'. 'Vella' has the meaning of movement. 'Pekha' has the meaning of movement, from which comes 'pekhito'.

Dvayaṃ nisite. Nisi nisāne. Tija nisāne, nisānaṃ tikkhakaraṇaṃ, ubhayatrāpi kammani to.

Two terms for 'sharpened'. From 'nisi', to sharpen. From 'tija', to sharpen; sharpening means making sharp. In both cases, the suffix 'ta' is used in the passive sense.

745-746. Tikaṃ pattabbe. Pata gamane, tabbo. Gamu gatiyaṃ, ṇyo, myassa mmo vā, gammaṃ, gamyaṃ, dyassa jjo, āpajjaṃ.

745-746. Three terms for 'to be attained'. From 'pata', to go, with the suffix 'tabba'. From 'gamu', to go, with the suffix 'ṇya', where 'my' optionally becomes 'mm', giving 'gammaṃ' or 'gamyaṃ'; and 'dy' becomes 'jj', giving 'āpajjaṃ'.

Dvayaṃ pariṇate. Pacino anekatthattā iha pariṇatattho. Namu namane, bhūvādi, kattari to, samā dve tulyatthā.

Two terms for 'matured' or 'developed'. The root 'paci', due to its various meanings, here has the meaning 'matured'. From 'namu', to bend, of the bhūvādi group, with the suffix 'ta' in the active voice; the two terms are similar in meaning.

Pañcakaṃ veṭhite. Veṭha veṭhane. Valamiva valayaṃ, kuṇḍalākāraṃ valayaṃ kataṃ valayitaṃ, nāmadhātu, kāritantā to. Rudha āvaraṇe, ruddhaṃ. Saṃpubbo vu saṃvaraṇe, saṃvutaṃ. Samantato vutaṃ āvutaṃ, vu saṃvaraṇe, sabbatra kammani to.

Five terms for 'enveloped' or 'wrapped'. From 'veṭha', to envelop. Like a bracelet, 'valaya' means a ring; made in the shape of a ring is 'valayita', from a nominal root, with the suffix 'ta' from the causative stem. From 'rudha', to obstruct, comes 'ruddhaṃ'. From 'vu', to restrain, with the prefix 'saṃ-', comes 'saṃvutaṃ'. Covered all around is 'āvutaṃ', from 'vu', to restrain; in all cases, the suffix 'ta' is used in the passive sense.

Dvayaṃ [M 0.0484] parikhādinā parikkhitte. Pari samantato karīyateti parikkhittaṃ, parikkhatampi. Vu saṃvaraṇe, nivutaṃ.

Two terms for being surrounded by a moat. 'Parikkhittaṃ' means made all around; also 'parikkhataṃ'. From the root 'vu', in the sense of covering, comes 'nivutaṃ'.

Tikaṃ vitthate. Sara gatiyaṃ, to, tassa ṭo, ralopo, visaṭaṃ. Tanu vitthāre, to, tassa to, nalopo, vitthataṃ, tataṃ.

Three terms for spreading. From the root 'sara', in the sense of movement, with the suffix 'ta', which becomes 'ṭa', and with elision of 'r' and 'l', comes 'visaṭaṃ'. From the root 'tanu', in the sense of spreading, with the suffix 'ta', and with elision of 'n' and 'l', come 'vitthataṃ' and 'tataṃ'.

Dvayaṃ lepanīye. Lipa lepane, diha upalepane, ubhayatrāpi kammani to.

Two terms for what is to be smeared. The root 'lipa' is in the sense of smearing, and 'diha' is in the sense of anointing; in both cases, the suffix 'ta' is used in the passive sense.

Dvayaṃ guḷhe. Guha saṃvaraṇe, ḷo, guḷho. Gupa gopane, gutto.

Two terms for 'concealed'. From the root 'guha', in the sense of covering, comes 'guḷha'. From the root 'gupa', in the sense of protecting, comes 'gutta'.

Dvayaṃ posanīye. Pusa posane, to, satānaṃ ṭṭho, ṭṭhābhāve posito.

Two terms for what is to be nourished. From the root 'pusa', in the sense of nourishing, with the suffix 'ta': the 's' and 't' become 'ṭṭha' (forming 'puṭṭha'); in the absence of 'ṭṭha', it is 'posito'.

747. Dvayaṃ salajje. Lajja pīḷe, pīḷo lajjāva. Hīḷa nindālajjāsu, hīḷito.

747. Two terms for being ashamed. The root 'lajja' is in the sense of oppressing; oppression is indeed shame. The root 'hīḷa' is in the sense of blame and shame, forming 'hīḷito'.

Dvayaṃ sadde. Sana dhana sadde, sanitaṃ, dhanitaṃ.

Two terms for sound. The roots 'sana' and 'dhana' are in the sense of sound; they form 'sanitaṃ' and 'dhanitaṃ'.

Pañcakaṃ bandhanīye. Sandanaṃ bandhanaṃ, taṃyogā vantu. Sandānavantaṃ kataṃ sandānitaṃ, nāmadhātumhā to, vantulopo. Sandānaṃ sajjā, tamassāti vā, ito. Si bandhane, to. Bandha bandhane, baddho. Kīla bandhane. Yamu uparame, saṃpubbo bandhane, sabbatra kammani to. Mūtaṃ, udditaṃ, sadditampi. Mū bandhane. Dā avakhaṇḍane. U saṃpubbo bandhane. Vuttañca “uddānantu ca bandhana”nti.

Five terms for what is to be bound. 'Sandanaṃ' is binding; from its connection with the suffix 'vantu', 'sandānavantaṃ' is made 'sandānitaṃ' from a nominal root, with the suffix 'ta' and elision of 'vantu'. 'Sandānaṃ' also means preparation, or 'one who has it', forming 'ito'. The root 'si' is in the sense of binding, with the suffix 'ta'. The root 'bandha' is in the sense of binding, forming 'baddho'. The root 'kīla' is in the sense of binding. The root 'yamu' is in the sense of restraint; with the prefix 'saṃ-', it is in the sense of binding; in all cases, the suffix 'ta' is used in the passive sense. Also 'mūtaṃ', 'udditaṃ', and 'sadditaṃ'. The root 'mū' is in the sense of binding. The root 'dā' is in the sense of breaking. The root 'u' with the prefix 'saṃ-' is in the sense of binding. And it is said: 'uddāna is also binding'.

748. Tikaṃ [M 0.0485] siddhe. Sidha saṃsiddhimhi. Pada gamane, nipubbo siddhiyaṃ. Vatta vattane, vattanaṃpyatra sijjhanaṃ nipubbattā.

748. Three terms for 'accomplished'. The root 'sidha' is in the sense of complete accomplishment. The root 'pada' is in the sense of going; with the prefix 'ni-', it is in the sense of accomplishment. The root 'vatta' is in the sense of turning; here 'vattanaṃ' also means accomplishment because it is preceded by 'ni-'.

Tikaṃ vidārite. Dara bhida vidāraṇe, innādeso. Bhinnaṃ. Aninnādese tu bheditaṃ.

Three terms for 'split'. The roots 'dara' and 'bhida' are in the sense of splitting; with the substitution of 'inna', it forms 'bhinnaṃ'. But when there is no substitution of 'inna', it forms 'bheditaṃ'.

Dvayaṃ tiṇādīhi chādanīye. Chada saṃvaraṇe, to, tassa sadhātvantassa annādeso.

Two terms for what is to be covered with grass, etc. The root 'chada' is in the sense of covering; with the suffix 'ta', the final consonant of the root together with the suffix becomes 'anna'.

Tikaṃ chindite. Vidha vedhane. Chidda kaṇṇabhede, curādi. Vidha vedhane, sabbatra kamme to, aparadvaye ca sañjātatthe ito.

Three terms for 'cut'. The root 'vidha' is in the sense of piercing. The root 'chidda', of the curādi class, is in the sense of splitting the ear. The root 'vidha' is in the sense of piercing. In all cases, the suffix 'ta' is used in the passive sense; and in the other two, the suffix 'ita' is used in the sense of 'having become'.

749. Tikaṃ ānīte. Hara haraṇe, bhara dhāraṇaposanesu, āpubbo nī naye.

749. Three terms denote 'brought.' The root hara is in the sense of 'carrying,' bhara in the senses of 'bearing' and 'nourishing,' and the root nī with the prefix ā in the sense of 'leading'.

Dvayaṃ damayutte. Damu damane, kattari to. Pakkamādīhi nto. Antādese damito. Kammasādhanopyayaṃ.

Two terms denote 'tamed.' The root damu is in the sense of 'taming'; the suffix ta is in the agentive sense. With pakkama and others, the suffix is nta. With the substitution of ita, it becomes damita. This is also formed in the objective sense.

Dvayaṃ sante. Samu upasame, kattarito. Antādese samito, kammasādhanopyayaṃ.

Two terms denote 'tranquil.' The root samu is in the sense of 'tranquility'; the suffix ta is in the agentive sense. With the substitution of ita, it becomes samita; this is also formed in the objective sense.

Dvayaṃ puṇṇe. Pūra pūraṇe, tarādīhi iṇṇo, dvīsupi kattukammasādhanāni labbhanti.

Two terms denote 'full.' The root pūra is in the sense of 'filling'; with the tarādi group of roots, the suffix is iṇṇa. In both cases, agentive and objective formations are obtained.

750. Tipādaṃ [M 0.0486] pūjite. Cāya pūjānisāmanesu. Maha pūjāyaṃ, pūja pūjane, araha pūjāyaṃ, arahito. Acca pūjāyaṃ. Māna pūjāyaṃ. Ci caye, apapubbo pūjane. Namassitopi, namassadhātu pūjāyaṃ.

750. Three terms denote 'honored.' The root cāya is in the senses of 'honoring' and 'observing.' The root maha is in the sense of 'honoring'; pūja in the sense of 'honoring'; araha in the sense of 'honoring,' forming arahita. The root acca is in the sense of 'honoring.' The root māna is in the sense of 'honoring.' The root ci is in the sense of 'gathering'; with the prefix apa, it is in the sense of 'honoring.' Also namassita; the root namassa is in the sense of 'honoring'.

Dvayaṃ tacchite dāruādimhi. Taccha tanukaraṇe, tanukarīyateti tanūkato, dīgho.

Two terms denote 'carved' in wood and so forth. The root taccha is in the sense of 'thinning'; because it is made thin, it is called tanūkata, with lengthening.

751. Dvayaṃ aggiādīhi tatte. Tapa dhūpa santāpe.

751. Two terms denote 'heated' by fire and so forth. The roots tapa and dhūpa are in the sense of 'heating' or 'scorching'.

Dvayaṃ rājādīnaṃ santike bhajanādivasena upagate. Cara gatyattho, upacarito. Āsa upavesane, upāsito.

Two terms denote 'approached' in the vicinity of kings and so forth, by way of service and so forth. The root cara has the meaning of 'going,' forming upacarita. The root āsa is in the sense of 'sitting,' forming upāsita.

Addhaṃ cute. Bhasa adhopatane, to. Gaḷa secane, gaḷitaṃ. Pada gamane, pannaṃ. Cu cavane, cu gamane vā. Dhaṃsu avasaṃsane, gatiyañca. Kannampi, kanna gatisosanesu.

Certainly, in the sense of 'fallen.' The root bhasa is in the sense of 'falling down,' with the suffix ta. The root gaḷa is in the sense of 'dripping,' forming gaḷita. The root pada is in the sense of 'going,' forming panna. The root cu is in the sense of 'moving' or 'going.' The root dhaṃsu is in the senses of 'perishing' and 'going.' Also kanna; the root kanna is in the senses of 'going' and 'drying up'.

752. Tuṭṭhantaṃ pamudite, pī tappanakantīsu. Muda hāse. Hasa haṃsane, hasa alike vā. Mada hāse, matto. Tusa pītiyaṃ.

752. Terms for 'delighted' and 'joyful.' The root pī is in the senses of 'satisfaction' and 'shining.' The root muda is in the sense of 'joy' or 'laughter.' The root hasa is in the sense of 'laughing,' or hasa in the sense of 'falsehood.' The root mada is in the sense of 'joy' or 'laughter,' forming matta. The root tusa is in the sense of 'joy' or 'satisfaction'.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0487] chinne. Kanta chedane. Chidi dvidhākaraṇe. Lū chedane, ṇo, yu vā. Dā lavane, tu, dā avakhaṇḍane vā. Chātampi. Cho chedane, ossākāro.

Four terms denote 'cut.' The root kanta is in the sense of 'cutting.' The root chidi is in the sense of 'dividing into two.' The root lū is in the sense of 'cutting,' with the suffix ṇa or yu. The root dā is in the sense of 'reaping,' with the suffix ta, or dā is in the sense of 'breaking apart.' Also chāta. The root cho is in the sense of 'cutting,' taking the form ossa.

Tikaṃ pasatthe. Saṭha thutiyaṃ, to. Vaṇṇa vaṇṇakriyāvitthāraguṇavacanesu. Thu abhitthave. Īḍito, paṇitopi, īḍa thutimhi. Paṇa byavahāre, thutimhi ca, paṇito.

Three terms denote 'praised.' The root saṭha is in the sense of 'praise,' with the suffix ta. The root vaṇṇa is in the senses of 'describing,' 'expounding,' and 'speaking of qualities.' The root thu is in the sense of 'praising.' Also īḍita and paṇita; the root īḍa is in the sense of 'praise.' The root paṇa is in the senses of 'transaction' and 'praise,' forming paṇita.

753. Pañcakaṃ alle, tima addabhāve niccalepi, pakkamādīhi nto. Alla kledane, lo, allaṃ. Adda gatimhi, yācane ca, āpubbo dā avakhaṇḍane vā, do, addaṃ. Kilida addabhāve, innādeso. Unda kledane, inno, unno vā, sāddampi. Addaguṇayuttaṃ addaṃ, tena saha vattate sāddaṃ.

753. Five terms denote 'wet.' The root tima is in the sense of 'wetness,' and also 'immobility'; with pakkama and others, the suffix is nta. The root alla is in the sense of 'wetting,' with the suffix la, forming alla. The root adda is in the senses of 'going' and 'begging'; or, the root dā with the prefix ā is in the sense of 'breaking apart,' with the suffix da, forming adda. The root kilida is in the sense of 'wetness,' with the substitution of inna. The root unda is in the sense of 'wetting,' with the suffix inna or unna; also sādda. Adda is that which is endowed with the quality of wetness; sādda is that which exists together with that.

Catukkaṃ gavesite. Magga anvesane, curādi. Esa gatiyaṃ, bhūvādi. Gavesa maggane, curādi.

Four terms denote 'sought.' The root magga is in the sense of 'seeking,' belonging to the curādi class. The root esa is in the sense of 'going,' belonging to the bhūvādi class. The root gavesa is in the sense of 'seeking,' belonging to the curādi class.

Dvayaṃ laddhe. Labha pattiyaṃ. Papubbo āpa byāpane, to, bhujādi, ālopo, pattaṃ. Bhāvitaṃ, āsāditaṃ, vibhūtañca.

Two terms denote 'obtained.' The root labha is in the sense of 'obtaining.' The root āpa with the prefix pa is in the sense of 'pervading'; with the suffix ta, belonging to the bhujādi class, and with elision of ā, it becomes patta. Also bhāvita, āsādita, and vibhūta.

754. Pālitantaṃ rakkhanīye, rakkha pālane. Gupa gopane, bhujādi. Tā pālane, tātaṃ. Āyāgame gopāyitaṃ. Ava rakkhaṇe, avitaṃ.

754. The group of terms for 'protected' are in the sense of 'what is to be guarded.' The root rakkha is in the sense of 'protecting.' The root gupa is in the sense of 'guarding,' belonging to the bhujādi class. The root tā is in the sense of 'protecting,' forming tāta. In the sense of 'coming,' it forms gopāyita. The root ava is in the sense of 'protecting,' forming avita.

Catukkaṃ [M 0.0488] catte. Saja vissagge. Caja hāniyaṃ. Hā cāge, ino, dīghādi, hīno. Ujha ussagge, samujjhitaṃ. Dhūtampi, dhū kampane.

Four terms denote 'given up.' The root saja is in the sense of 'releasing.' The root caja is in the sense of 'abandoning' or 'loss.' The root hā is in the sense of 'abandoning'; with the suffix ina, lengthening, and so forth, it becomes hīna. The root ujha is in the sense of 'casting off,' forming samujjhita. Also dhūta; the root dhū is in the sense of 'shaking'.

755. Pajjaṃ bhāsite. Bhāsa byattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ. Lapa byattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vaca bhāsane, vuttaṃ. Abhipubbo dhā dhāraṇe, to, dhātissa hi, hi gamane vā, abhihitaṃ. Khyā kathane. Jappa byattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ. Īra khepagativacanakampanesu, udīritaṃ. Katha vākyapabandhe. Gada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ. Bhaṇa bhaṇane. Vada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, to, vassu, uditaṃ.

755. A group of terms for 'spoken.' The root bhāsa is in the sense of 'clear speech.' The root lapa is in the sense of 'clear speech'; vaca is in the sense of 'speaking,' forming vutta. The root dhā with the prefix abhi is in the sense of 'holding'; with the suffix ta, and the substitution of hi for the root, or from the root hi in the sense of 'going,' it becomes abhihita. The root khyā is in the sense of 'telling.' The root jappa is in the sense of 'clear speech.' The root īra is in the senses of 'throwing,' 'going,' 'speaking,' and 'trembling,' forming udīrita. The root katha is in the sense of 'composing sentences.' The root gada is in the sense of 'clear speech.' The root bhaṇa is in the sense of 'speaking.' The root vada is in the sense of 'clear speech,' with the suffix ta, and vassu, forming udita.

756. Catukkaṃ avamānite. Ñā avabodhane. Gaṇa saṅkhyāne. Bhū sattāyaṃ. Māna pūjāyaṃ, mana ñāṇe vā, avaparipubbā ete paribhūte. Heṭṭhā katvā ñāyati, gaṇīyati, maññatīti avaññito, avagaṇito, avamānito ca. Paribhavīyati avamānaṃ karīyatīti paribhūto.

756. Four terms denote 'despised.' The root ñā is in the sense of 'understanding.' The root gaṇa is in the sense of 'counting.' The root bhū is in the sense of 'being' or 'existence.' The root māna is in the sense of 'honoring,' or mana in the sense of 'knowing'; these, when prefixed by ava and pari, mean 'despised.' Because one knows, counts, or thinks of someone as inferior, they are called avaññita, avagaṇita, and avamānita. Because one is treated with contempt, one is called paribhūta.

Catukkaṃ chāte. Ghasa adane, cho, dvittaṃ. Jighacchā sañjātā yassa jighacchito. Khuda pipāsāyaṃ. Chāda bhakkhane. Bhuja pālanajjhohāresu, kho, dvittādi, bubhukkhā sañjātā yassa bubhukkhito.

Four terms denote 'hungry.' The root ghasa is in the sense of 'eating'; with the substitution of cha and doubling. One in whom hunger (jighacchā) has arisen is jighacchita. The root khud is in the sense of 'thirst.' The root chāda is in the sense of 'eating.' The root bhuja is in the senses of 'nourishing' and 'ingesting'; with the substitution of kha, doubling, and so forth; one in whom hunger (bubhukkhā) has arisen is bubhukkhita.

757. Chakkaṃ [M 0.0489] ñāte. Budha ñā avagamane. Pada gamane, to, tassa anno, paṭipannaṃ. Vida ñāṇe. Gati bujhattho. Avagataṃ. Mana ñāṇe, to, mataṃ.

757. Six terms denote 'known.' The roots budh and ñā are in the sense of 'understanding.' The root pad is in the sense of 'going'; with the suffix ta, its t becomes ṇṇa, forming paṭipanna. The root vid is in the sense of 'knowing.' The root gam has the meaning of 'understanding.' Also avagata. The root man is in the sense of 'knowing,' with the suffix ta, forming mata.

Addhaṃ gilite. Gala adane, assi, gilito. Khāda bhakkhane. Bhuja pālanajjhohāresu. Bhakkha adane. Adhiavapubbo hara haraṇe, to, tassa ṭo, ralopo, ajjhohaṭo. Asa bhakkhane, asito. Jappito, gasitopi, jappa adane. Gasa adane.

Certainly, in the sense of 'swallowed.' The root gal is in the sense of 'eating'; with the suffix ita, it becomes gilita. The root khād is in the sense of 'eating.' The root bhuj is in the senses of 'nourishing' and 'ingesting.' The root bhakkh is in the sense of 'eating.' The root har with the prefixes adhi and ava is in the sense of 'carrying'; with the suffix ta, its t becomes ṭa, and with the elision of ra, it becomes ajjhohaṭa. The root as is in the sense of 'eating,' forming asita. Also jappita and gasita; the root japp is in the sense of 'eating.' The root gas is in the sense of 'eating'.

Visesyādhīnavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the explanation of the section on terms dependent on the qualified noun.

2. Saṃkiṇṇavaggavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Miscellaneous Section

758. Pubbasmiṃ [M 0.0490] kaṇḍadvaye buddhādīni nāmāni samānatthāni pakaraṇena nibaddhāni, asmimpi kaṇḍe sobhanādīni visesananāmāni, samayādīnyanekatthāni, cirassamādīni ca abyayāni pakaraṇeneva nibaddhāni, idāni pana pubbavaggesu vitthārabhayā ye na nibaddhā, taṃsaṅgahatthaṃ, taṃsamayānupālanatthañca saṃkiṇṇamārabhate “ñe yya”miccādinā. Tassattho – ihāpi saṃkiṇṇavaggepi kvāpi katthaci kriyādīsu paccayatthavasena āpaccayādīnaṃ itthiliṅgādibhāvajotakassa sabhāvassa vasena liṅgaṃ itthiliṅgādikaṃ ñeyyanti. Cakārena bhiyyo rūpantarādipariggahopi. Ihāti ca upalakkhaṇaṃ, vaggantaresupi paccayatthavasena liṅgādinicchayasambhavato.

758. In the two previous sections, nouns such as 'Buddha' which have similar meanings were arranged by topic. In this section as well, adjectives such as 'Sobhana,' polysemous words such as 'samaya,' and indeclinables such as 'cirassam' are also arranged by topic. Now, however, for the purpose of collecting those terms not included in the previous sections for fear of prolixity, and for the purpose of maintaining that convention, the miscellaneous section is begun with 'ñeyya,' and so forth. Its meaning is as follows: here, in this miscellaneous section, in some cases concerning actions and so forth, the gender—feminine and so on—should be understood based on the meaning of the suffix, and based on the inherent nature of suffixes such as ā which indicate feminine gender. The word ca also implies the inclusion of further variant forms and the like. And 'here' is merely indicative, since in other sections too, the determination of gender and so forth is possible based on the meaning of the suffix.

Kattabbato kriyā, kara karaṇe, ṇyo, ikārāgamo, assi, vaṇṇavipariyaye kriyā, kriyampi, ririyapaccaye kiriyaṃ, kiriyāpi. Rammapaccaye kammaṃ.

Kriyā (action) is so called from the sense of 'what is to be done.' The root kar is in the sense of 'doing'; with the suffix ṇya, the augment i, and by metathesis of letters, it becomes kriyā, and also kriya. With the suffix ririya, it becomes kiriya or kiriyā. With the suffix ramma, it becomes kamma.

Tikaṃ cittopasame. Samu upasame,ti, santi. Thamhi samatho. Amhi samo.

A triad of terms for 'calming of the mind.' The root sam is in the sense of 'calming'; with the suffix ti, it becomes santi. With the suffix tha, it becomes samatha. With the suffix a, it becomes sama.

Tikaṃ kāyopasame. Damu upasame. Thamhi damatho. Timhi danti. Cittopasamepyete.

A triad of terms for 'calming of the body.' The root dam is in the sense of 'calming.' With the suffix tha, it becomes damatha. With the suffix ti, it becomes danti. These also apply to the calming of the mind.

Suddhakammani vattaṃ bhavati. Vatta vattane, vatta samādāne vā vattaṃ, asītimahāvattādi.

Vatta occurs in the sense of pure action. The root vat is in the sense of 'occurring' or 'undertaking'; hence vatta, as in the eighty great practices and so forth.

Āsaṅgavacanaṃ āsattavacanaṃ saddasarūpaṃ parāyaṇaṃ nāma vuttaṃ, tañca tīsu. Paraṃ āyanaṃ āyatto tāṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ, kammāsatto iccattho, sākalyavacane tu pārāyaṇaṃ, pāraṃ pariyantaṃ ayanti gacchanti kassaci anenāti pārāyaṇaṃ, yu, ṇattaṃ, yathā – nāmapārāyaṇaṃ, dhātupārāyaṇaṃ.

The word-form parāyaṇa is said to be a term for 'attachment' and 'dependence,' and it occurs in three genders. Parāyaṇa is derived from paraṃ āyanaṃ ('going to another'), meaning 'dependent' or 'protection'; the sense is 'attached to action.' In the sense of completeness, however, it is pārāyaṇa. Pārāyaṇa is that by which one goes to the far shore (pāra) or limit (pariyanta). The suffixes are yu and ṇa, as in nāmapārāyaṇa (a complete recitation of names) and dhātupārāyaṇa (a complete recitation of roots).

759. Tikaṃ [M 0.0491] dvidhābhāve. Bhidi dvidhākaraṇe, ṇo. Dara vidāraṇe. Phuṭa vikasane, phuṭa bhedane vā, yu.

759. The triad [of terms] is in the sense of twofold division. The root 'bhidi' is in the sense of 'dividing in two'; [with the affix] 'ṇo'. The root 'dara' is in the sense of 'tearing'. The root 'phuṭa' is in the sense of 'opening' or 'breaking'; [with the affix] 'yu'.

Dvayaṃ tappane. Tapa pīṇane, yu. Pī tappane, yu, kiyādi, nassa ṇattaṃ. Avanampi, ava pālane, dittiyañca anekatthattā.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of satisfying. The root 'tapa' is in the sense of 'pleasing'; [with the affix] 'yu'. The root 'pī' is in the sense of 'satisfying'; [with the affix] 'yu', [it belongs to the] kiyādi [group of roots], the 'n' becomes 'ṇ'. And 'avana' [is derived from] the root 'ava' in the sense of 'protecting' and also 'shining', due to having multiple meanings.

Dvayaṃ sāpe. Kusa avhāne, bhedane ca, yu. Sanja saṅge, abhisaṅgo.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of a curse or oath. The root 'kusa' is in the sense of 'calling' and 'breaking'; [with the affix] 'yu'. The root 'sanja' is in the sense of 'connection'; [hence] 'abhisaṅgo'.

Tikaṃ yācanāyaṃ. Bhikkha yācane, yu. Yāca yācane. Attha yācane. Addanopyatra, adda gatimhi, yācane ca.

The triad [of terms] is in the sense of requesting. The root 'bhikkha' is in the sense of 'requesting'; [with the affix] 'yu'. The root 'yāca' is in the sense of 'requesting'. The root 'attha' is in the sense of 'requesting'. And 'addana' is also here; the root 'adda' is in the sense of 'going' and 'requesting'.

760. Nimittarahitaṃ yadicchā nāma, yā yā icchā adhippāyo yadicchā nāma. Seritāpi.

760. That which is devoid of a cause is called 'yadicchā'; whatever wish or intention is called 'yadicchā'. Also 'seritā'.

Tikaṃ āpucchane, āpucchanañca gamanāgamanādisamaye suhajja bandhavādīnamāliṅgana cumbanasvāgatapiyavacanārogyapucchanagamanānuññādinā ānandanaṃ. Puccha pucchane, āpucchanaṃ. Nanda samiddhiyaṃ, ānandanaṃ. Sabhāja pītidassanesu, sabhāja pītivacanesu vā, curādi, yu, sabhājanaṃ.

The triad [of terms] is in the sense of taking leave. And 'āpucchana' is the delighting of friends, relatives, and others at times of coming, going, and so forth, by means of embracing, kissing, welcoming, affectionate words, asking after health, granting permission to leave, and the like. The root 'puccha' is in the sense of 'asking'; [hence] 'āpucchanaṃ'. The root 'nanda' is in the sense of 'prosperity'; [hence] 'ānandanaṃ'. The root 'sabhāja' is in the sense of 'showing affection' or 'affectionate words'; [it belongs to the] curādi [group of roots]; [with the affix] 'yu', [it becomes] 'sabhājanaṃ'.

Dvayaṃ naye. Ñāyanti yenāti ñāyo, ākārantānamāyo. Nyāyopi, nissesato ayati yena nyāyo. Nī naye, ayādeso, nayo.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of leading. 'Ñāyo' is that by which they are led; for those [roots] ending in 'ā', [it becomes] 'āyo'. And also 'nyāyo'; 'nyāyo' is that by which one goes completely. The root 'nī' is in the sense of 'leading'; with the substitution of 'aya', [it becomes] 'nayo'.

Dvayaṃ [M 0.0492] vuddhimhi. Phā vuddhimhi, phāya vuddhiyaṃ vā, yalopo,ti, phāti, nāriyaṃ. Vaddha vaddhane,ti, dalopo, dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā ca, assu, vuddhi, vuḍḍhipi.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of growth. The root 'phā' is in the sense of 'growth', or 'phāya' in the sense of 'growth'; by elision of 'ya', with the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'phāti', [which is] feminine. The root 'vaddha' is in the sense of 'increasing'; with the affix 'ti', by elision of 'da', and by the rule 'dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā ca, assu', [it becomes] 'vuddhi', and also 'vuḍḍhi'.

761. Kilama hāsakkhaye, tho, kilamatho. Yumhi kilamanaṃ. Sū pāṇipasave, pasavanaṃ pasavo, timhi pasūti.

761. The root 'kilama' is in the sense of 'exhaustion' or 'decline'; with the affix 'tho', [it becomes] 'kilamatho'. With the affix 'yu', [it becomes] 'kilamanaṃ'. The root 'sū' is in the sense of 'giving birth to living beings'; 'pasavanaṃ' [is] 'pasavo'; with the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'pasūti'.

Kasa gatiyaṃ hiṃsāyañca, niggahītāgamo, ukkaṃso, kasa vilekhane vā. Atisayo vutto. Bhusādayo pamāṇātisayavasena vuttā, ukkaṃso guṇātisayavasena vutto, atisayo pana ubhayavasenāti ubhayatra niddiṭṭhānaṃ bhedo. Tikaṃ jayane. Jayanaṃ jayo, yu, jayanaṃ. Timhi jiti, nārī.

The root 'kasa' is in the sense of 'movement' and 'harming'; with the niggahīta augment, [it becomes] 'ukkaṃso'; or the root 'kasa' is in the sense of 'scratching'. 'Atisayo' is mentioned. Words like 'bhusā' are said by way of excess of measure; 'ukkaṃso' is said by way of excess of quality; 'atisayo', however, is said by way of both; thus is the distinction of those indicated in both senses. The triad [of terms] is in the sense of conquering. 'Jayanaṃ' [is] 'jayo'; with the affix 'yu', [it becomes] 'jayanaṃ'. With the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'jiti', [which is] feminine.

762. Bandhanantāni dve dve nāmāni. Vasa kantiyaṃ. Kamu kantiyaṃ,ti. Vidha vedhane, byathane ca anekatthattā, a, ikārassa yādeso, byadho, vedho. Gaha upādāne nibandhane ca, gaho, gāho ca. Vara āvaraṇe, varo. Vu saṃvaraṇe,ti, vuti. Paca pāke, itthiyamatiyavo vā, a. Pacanaṃ pāko, ṇo.

762. Two by two, the names ending in 'bandhana'. The root 'vasa' is in the sense of 'desiring'. The root 'kamu' is in the sense of 'desiring'; [with the affix] 'ti'. The root 'vidha' is in the sense of 'piercing' and 'afflicting', due to having multiple meanings; with the affix 'a', and the substitution of 'ya' for 'i', [it becomes] 'byadho' and 'vedho'. The root 'gaha' is in the sense of 'grasping' and 'binding'; [hence] 'gaho' and 'gāho'. The root 'vara' is in the sense of 'covering'; [hence] 'varo'. The root 'vu' is in the sense of 'restraining'; with the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'vuti'. The root 'paca' is in the sense of 'cooking'; in the feminine, [with the affix] 'atiyavo' or 'a'. 'Pacanaṃ' [is also] 'pāko'; [the latter is formed with the affix] 'ṇo'.

Dvayaṃ āhvāne. Hu dānādanahabyappadānesu, ṇo, havo. Timhi huti. Dvayaṃ anubhavane. Vida ñāṇe, ṇo, vedo[M 0.0493]. Vida vedanākhyānanivāsesu, curādi, yu, vedanaṃ, vākāro vedanāsaddassa napuṃsakattāpekkho.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of calling. The root 'hu' is in the sense of 'giving', 'taking', and 'offering oblations'; with the affix 'ṇo', [it becomes] 'havo'. With the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'huti'. The pair [of terms] is in the sense of experiencing. The root 'vida' is in the sense of 'knowing'; with the affix 'ṇo', [it becomes] 'vedo'. The root 'vida' is in the sense of 'declaring feelings' and 'dwelling'; [it belongs to the] curādi [group of roots]; with the affix 'yu', [it becomes] 'vedanaṃ'. The particle 'vā' is with reference to the neuter gender of the word 'vedanā'.

763. Dvayaṃ dhanādijāniyaṃ. Jara vayohānimhi, yu, jīraṇaṃ, assī. Hā cāge, yu, nadādi, rasso, hassa jo, jāni. Tā pālane, yu, ṇattaṃ. Dvayaṃ pamāṇe. Mā māne,ti, pamiti. Amhi pamā.

763. The pair [of terms] is in the sense of 'loss of wealth etc.'. The root 'jara' is in the sense of 'decline of age'; with the affix 'yu', [it becomes] 'jīraṇaṃ'; [with the affix] 'assī'. The root 'hā' is in the sense of 'giving up'; with the affix 'yu', [it belongs to the] nadādi [group of roots], with shortening, 'ha' becomes 'ja', [it becomes] 'jāni'. The root 'tā' is in the sense of 'protecting'; with the affix 'yu', [and] the change to 'ṇ'. The pair [of terms] is in the sense of measure. The root 'mā' is in the sense of 'measuring'; with the affix 'ti', [it becomes] 'pamiti'. With the affix 'a', [it becomes] 'pamā'.

Dvayaṃ saṃyoge. Silisa āliṅgane. Saṃpubbo dhā dhāraṇe, i, sandhanaṃ sandhi. Dvayaṃ khaye. Khi khaye, ṇo, isse, e aya, khayo. Ci caye, apapubbo khaye. Dvayaṃ sadde. Ru sadde, ṇo, vuddhyādeso. Raṇa sadde. A, raṇo.

The pair [of terms] is in the sense of joining. The root 'silisa' is in the sense of 'embracing'.
