Bhabba: in the sense of one capable and worthy of liberation, and in what is to be. Guṇādhāra: in the sense of a repository or basis of virtue. Vitta: in the sense of wealth or riches. Budha: in the sense of the wise or learned. Dāru: a log of wood.

914. Patthādo pattho, tulā, aṅgulīti patthādi. Vidhāya unnatiyaṃ. Parissame khede.

914. Patthādi: a group of measures such as pattha, tulā, and aṅgulī. Vidhā: in the sense of elevation. Parissama: in the sense of exertion or fatigue.

915. Saroruhe kamale. Khagantare rukkhakimikhādakasakuṇe. Tūriyantare vaṃsasaṅkhādike.

915. Saroruha: in the sense of a lotus. Khagantara: in the sense of a bird that eats tree-insects. Tūriyantara: in the sense of musical instruments such as bamboo flutes, conches, and so on.

916. Saṃvege ubbege, vimhaye ca.

916. Saṃvega: in the sense of agitation, dismay, and astonishment.

917. Tadupetanisāya candappabhāya yuttarattiyaṃ.

917. Tadupetanisā: a night endowed with the radiance of the moon.

918. Māse tatiyamāse. Ativuddhe ca atipasatthe ca.

918. In the sense of a month: the third month. And in the sense of very old and very excellent.

919. Nibandhe balakkāre “balaggaho”tyādīsu.

919. Nibandha: in the sense of binding or forcing, as in 'grasping strongly' and similar expressions.

Mattikābhedo nīlādivaṇṇayuttakittimamattikā. Sikkāyaṃ udakakumbhādivāhike. Nayanāmaye cakkhurogavisese.

Mattikābheda: a type of artificial clay endowed with blue and other colors. Sikkā: in the sense of a carrier for water pots and the like. Nayanāmaya: in the sense of a specific eye ailment.

920. Maṇḍale [M 0.0539] parimaṇḍale. Bimbikā latājāti, tassā phale ca bimbaṃ.

920. Maṇḍala: in the sense of a circle or perfectly round. Bimbikā: a creeping plant species, and its fruit is called bimba.

921. Pathe añjase.

921. Patha: in the sense of a direct path.

922. Santi nibbānaṃ. Nibhe sadise.

922. Santi: Nibbāna. Nibha: in the sense of similar or like.

Cāpe dhanumhi issāsaṃ. Usuno sarassa khepakamhi perake issāso.

The word `issāsa` is used for a bow (`cāpa`, `dhanu`). The word `issāso` is used for an archer, one who shoots an arrow (`usu`, `sara`).

923. Bālasaddo tīsu. Kutratthesu? Ādivayasā paṭhamavayena samaṅgini samannāgate ca. Apaṇḍite mūḷhe ca.

923. The word 'bāla' is used in three senses. In what meanings? In one endowed with the initial age, the first age; and in the unlearned and the deluded.

Soṇite lohite. Tambaṃ udumbaraṃ. Anuratto anurāgayutto puggalo. Rañjitaṃ raṅgarañjitaṃ.

Soṇita: in the sense of blood, gore. Tamba: in the sense of copper; the udumbara tree. Anuratta: a person endowed with attachment. Rañjita: dyed, colored with dye.

924. Viraḷe nirantare. Kise athūle. Hime tuhine.

924. Viraḷa: in the sense of continuous. Kisa: in the sense of lean or not stout. Hima: in the sense of ice or frost.

925. Guḷabhedo [M 0.0540] yo loke “sakkharā”ti vuccati. Kaṭhale silākhaṇḍe.

925. Guḷabheda: a type of sugar which is called 'sakkharā' in the world. Kaṭhala: in the sense of a stony or rocky fragment.

926. Tikhiṇe tikkhe. Byatte cheke. Rogamutte niroge.

926. Tikhiṇa: in the sense of sharp or keen. Byatta: in the sense of clever or skillful. Rogamutta: in the sense of free from disease or healthy.

Khattiye muddhābhisitte. Naranāthe tadaññasmiṃ. Pabhumhi issare.

Khattiya: in the sense of a consecrated sovereign of the Khattiya caste. Naranātha: in the sense of another such lord of men. Prabhu: in the sense of a master or lord.

927. Dhaññakaraṇaṃ dhaññamaddanaṭṭhānaṃ. Kakke nahānacuṇṇe. Nīce adhame. Setepi khalo.

927. Dhaññakaraṇa: a threshing floor, a place for treading out grain. Kakka: in the sense of sediment or bath powder. Nīca: in the sense of low or inferior. The word `khalo` is also used in the sense of white.

928. Brahmacārī ca gahaṭṭho ca vānappattho ca bhikkhu cāti brahmacārīgahaṭṭhādi, tapodhane piyasīle.

928. The term `brahmacārīgahaṭṭhādi` refers to the celibate, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the monk; it is also used in the sense of one rich in austerity, and one of pleasant virtue.

Kaṭhine kakkhaḷe. Niddaye nikkaruṇe.

Kaṭhina: in the sense of harsh or rough. Niddaya: in the sense of merciless or unkind.

929. Kaniṭṭho [M 0.0541] ca kaniyo cāti ete tīsu. Kutratthesu? Atyappe, atiyuvepi.

929. The words 'kaniṭṭha' and 'kaniya' are used in three senses. In what meanings? In very small, and in very young.

Iṭṭhe, nissāre ca agarumhi cāti etesvatthesu tīsu.

In these three meanings: desirable, unsubstantial, and not heavy.

930. Adhobhāge ca hīne ca. Dantacchade dantāvaraṇe.

930. In the sense of the lower part and the inferior. Dantacchada: in the sense of a tooth covering.

Pāricariyāyaṃ upaṭṭhāke.

In the sense of service (`pāricariyā`) and an attendant (`upaṭṭhāka`).

931. Ratane dvividatthike. Gaṇe samūhe yathā “kesahattho”ti. Soṇḍāya karikare. Bhantaraṃ terasamanakkhattaṃ.

931. In the sense of a cubit (`ratana`); a group (`gaṇa`) or multitude (`samūha`), as in `kesahattho`; an elephant's trunk (`soṇḍā`, `karikara`); and the thirteenth constellation (`bhantara`).

Āvāṭe kāsuyaṃ. Udapānaṃ andhu, yatra jalaṃ ghaṭiyantena uddharitvā pivanti.

Āvāṭa: in the sense of a pit (`kāsu`). Udapāna: a well (`andhu`), from which water is drawn up with a water-machine to drink.

932. Paṭhamaṃ pamukhañcāti idaṃ abhidhānadvayaṃ ādimhi padhāne vattati.

932. The two terms 'paṭhama' (first) and 'pamukha' (foremost) are used in the sense of beginning and principal.

Vajjabhedo ubhayatalaṃ tūriyaṃ.

A type of musical instrument (`vajjabheda`), specifically a double-sided (`ubhayatala`) instrument (`tūriya`).

933. Thiraṃso [M 0.0542] thirakoṭṭhāso.

933. Thiraṃsa: one whose parts are firm (`thirakoṭṭhāsa`).

Khandhabhāro khandhena vahitabbo bhāro. Ādinā kaṭibhārādayo gahitā. Yasmā palasataṃ tulā, vīsatitulā bhāro, tasmā “dvisahassapale”ti vuttaṃ.

Khandhabhāra: a burden to be carried on the shoulder. By 'ādi' (etc.), burdens carried on the hip and so on are included. Since one hundred palas make a tulā, and twenty tulās make a bhāra, therefore 'two thousand palas' is stated.

934. Mandire gehe. Rogabhede khayaroge. Apacayamhi viddhaṃsane, vināse ca.

934. In the sense of a house (`mandira`, `geha`); in the sense of a type of disease (`rogabheda`), namely consumption (`khayaroga`); and in the sense of decline (`apacaya`), that is, destruction (`viddhaṃsana`) and ruin (`vināsa`).

Sāpade byagghādike duṭṭhamige. Sappe urage. Kurūre kakkhaḷe.

In the sense of a beast of prey (`sāpada`), that is, a vicious wild animal such as a tiger; in the sense of a snake (`sappa`, `uraga`); and in the sense of cruel (`kurūra`) or harsh (`kakkhaḷa`).

935. Sajjadume assakaṇṇarukkhe. Rukkhe rukkhamatte.

935. In the sense of the Sal tree (`sajjaduma`, `assakaṇṇarukkha`), and in the sense of a tree in general (`rukkhamatta`).

Sote kaṇṇe. Yajane pūjane. Sutiyaṃ savanakriyāyaṃ.

In the sense of the ear (`sota`, `kaṇṇa`); in the sense of worship (`yajana`, `pūjana`); and in the sense of hearing (`suti`), that is, the act of listening (`savanakriyā`).

936. Peto [M 0.0543] ca paretocāti ime mate kālaṅkate ca petayonije petayonisambhave siyuṃ.

936. The words 'peta' and 'pareta' refer to the dead, those who have passed away, and those born in the realm of departed spirits, those who have arisen in the realm of departed spirits.

Khyāte pākaṭe. Haṭṭhe pahaṭṭhe.

In the sense of renowned (`khyāta`) or evident (`pākaṭa`), and in the sense of joyful (`haṭṭha`) or delighted (`pahaṭṭha`).

937. Adhippāye ajjhāsaye.

937. In the sense of intention (`adhippāya`) or disposition (`ajjhāsaya`).

Pakkhe sakuṇādīnaṃ pakkhe. Dale rukkhādīnaṃ chade. Bhājane lohamayādike. “Sogate”ti idaṃ “bhājane”ti imassa visesanaṃ. Sogate sugatassa santake bhājanetyattho.

In the sense of a wing (`pakkha`), such as the wing of a bird; in the sense of a leaf (`dala`), such as the covering of a tree; in the sense of a vessel (`bhājana`), made of metal and so forth. The word `sogate` is a qualifier for `bhājane`, meaning a vessel belonging to the Sugata.

938. Suṭṭhukate sammā kate kammani.

938. In the sense of a well-done action (`suṭṭhukata`), that is, an action properly performed (`sammā kata kamma`).

Anukampāyārahe dukkhitasatte.

In the sense of one worthy of compassion (`anukampāyāraha`), that is, a suffering being (`dukkhitasatta`).

939. Dhanimhi [M 0.0544] sadde.

939. Dhani: in the sense of sound.

940. Vihite vidhātabbe.

940. Vihita: in the sense of what is arranged and what is to be arranged.

Añjase magge. Visikhā racchā. Pantiyaṃ pāḷiyaṃ.

Añjasa: in the sense of a direct path. Visikhā: in the sense of a street. Panti: in the sense of a row or line.

941. Gagane ākāse. Byasane vipattiyaṃ.

941. Gagana: in the sense of the sky or space. Byasana: in the sense of calamity or misfortune.

Nettaroge cakkhurogavisese. Chadimhi gehādīnaṃ chadane.

Nettaroga: in the sense of a specific eye disease. Chadi: in the sense of the roof or covering of a house and the like.

942. Saṅghaṭṭane dvinnaṃ antarabhūte. Puna sandhīti padapūraṇatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Atisante atisamite.

942. Saṅghaṭṭana: in the sense of being in between two things. The phrase 'puna sandhi' is stated for the purpose of filling out the line. Atisanta: in the sense of very calm or very tranquil.

943. Yāpanā [M 0.0545] yāpanakārako kabaḷīkārāhāraraso. Ditti jalanaṃ. Balaṃ thāmo.

943. Yāpanā: sustenance; the sustaining nutritive essence of food in morsels. Ditti: in the sense of burning or flame. Bala: in the sense of strength or force.

944. Kucchi udaraṃ. Ovarako gehaviseso.

944. Kucchi: the belly or abdomen. Ovaraka: a particular type of dwelling; an inner chamber.

Khaṇḍane chedane. Itivutte ca kammanīti “iti evaṃ mayā pubbe carita”nti vattabbe subhāsubhakamme. “Ativatte ca kammanī”tipi pāṭho, atītakāle pavattakammanītyattho.

Khaṇḍana: in the sense of breaking or cutting. Itivutta: in the sense of actions, referring to good and bad deeds that are to be spoken of as, 'Thus was it done by me formerly.' There is also the reading 'ativatte kammani,' meaning actions performed in a past time.

945. Cittake nalāṭe katakāḷādibindumhi rukkhabhede marīcappamāṇambilarukkhe, yassa phalena ambilasūpaṃ pacanti. Tilakāḷake taṃtaṃsarīrāvayave sañjātatilasaṇṭhāne kāḷake.

945. Cittaka: in the sense of a mark made on the forehead, such as a black spot; also, a type of tree, a sour tree the size of a peppercorn, with whose fruit they cook sour soup. Tilakāḷaka: a black spot on some part of the body, having the shape of a sesame seed that has appeared there.

Bodhe bujjhane. Patti lābho, pāpuṇañca.

Bodha: in the sense of awakening or understanding. Patti: in the sense of gain and also attainment.

946. Āyumhi jīvite. Hadayaṅgānile urogamavāte.

946. Āyu: in the sense of life or lifespan. Hadayaṅgānila: in the sense of the heart-wind, the wind that moves in the chest.

Vase [M 0.0546] āyattatāyaṃ. Vede catubbidhavede. Icchā ārammaṇicchā.

Vasa: in the sense of being under control, dependence. Vede: in the sense of the fourfold Veda. Icchā: desire for an object.

947. Sirasaṭṭhimhi siraso aṭṭhimhi. Ghaṭādisakale ghaṭādikhaṇḍe.

947. Sirasaṭṭhi: in the sense of a bone of the head. Ghaṭādisakala: in the sense of a fragment of a pot or the like.

948. Veṇvādisākhājālasminti veṇuādīnañca aññamaññasaṃsagge sākhāsamūhe. Laggakese tāpasādīnaṃ laggakese. Ālaye taṇhāyaṃ.

948. Veṇvādisākhājāla: in the sense of a collection of branches of bamboo and the like, in mutual connection. Laggakesa: in the sense of the matted hair of ascetics and others. Ālaya: in the sense of craving.

Vadhe māraṇe. Rakkhitasmiṃ kammani, kattari ca.

Vadha: in the sense of killing or execution. Rakkhita: in the sense of the object of an action, and also the agent.

949. Thiyaṃ itthiyaṃ. Piye sāmike. Manuññe manaso tosanajanake. Gavakkhe sīhapañjare.

949. Thī: in the sense of a woman. Piya: in the sense of a husband. Manuñña: in the sense of that which generates satisfaction in the mind. Gavakkha: in the sense of a latticed window (sīhapañjara).

950. Kiṃ saddo pucchanatthādīsu saliṅgo. Vikappatthādīsu tu abyayaṃ.

950. The word 'kiṃ' has gender in the sense of questioning and so forth. However, in the sense of alternative and the like, it is an indeclinable.

Sasaddhe [M 0.0547] saddhāya sahite. Nivāpe petādīnaṃ kattabbapūjādāne. Paccaye saddahane saddhā.

Sasaddha: in the sense of one endowed with faith. Nivāpa: in the sense of an offering of worship to be made to the departed and others. Saddhā: in the sense of confidence or belief.

951. Aṭṭhismiṃ “panasabījaṃ tālabīja”ntyādīsu. Sukke ca bijaṃ.

951. Bīja: in the sense of a kernel, as in 'jackfruit seed, palm seed,' and so forth; and also in the sense of semen.

Pūye pakkavaṇasañjāte. Aggato purato. Disādo sūriyuggamanadisāyaṃ. Sā hi disānaṃ ādibhūtā, “disā”ti vā disāviseso. Ādinā pubbajādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ.

Pūya: in the sense of what has arisen from a festering wound. Aggato: in front of. Ādi: in the sense of the direction of the sun's rising, for that is the first of the directions; or it is a specific direction. By 'ādi' is meant the inclusion of the first-born and so forth.

952. Āgamane asantuppattikriyāyaṃ. Dīghādinikāyasmiṃ dīghanikāyamajjhimanikāyādike.

952. Āgamana: in the sense of the action of a non-existent thing coming into being. Dīghādinikāya: in the sense of the Dīgha Nikāya, Majjhima Nikāya, and the like.

953. Devarukkho sirīso. Santatiyaṃ vaṃse.

953. Devarukkha: the sirīsa tree. Santati: in the sense of continuity or lineage.

Uttaraviparīte aseṭṭhe, imasmiṃ atthe nakāro paṭisedhattho. Seṭṭhe uttame. Imasmiṃ atthe paṭisedhatthova nakāro. “Anu uttara”nti chedo ca viññeyyo.

Anuttara: in the sense opposite to 'superior,' that is, 'not the best,' wherein the particle 'na' has the meaning of negation. Also, in the sense of 'best' or 'highest,' wherein the particle 'na' also has the meaning of negation, i.e., there is none superior. And the analysis 'anu-uttara' should also be understood.

954. Sattisampattiyaṃ [M 0.0548] pabhāvādīhi sattīhi sampattiyaṃ. Kantimatte kamanīyamatte. Sūravīriyesupi vikkamo.

954. Sattisampatti: in the sense of the attainment of powers such as majesty. Kantimatta: in the sense of mere loveliness. Vikkama: also in the sense of the heroism and energy of heroes.

Paṭibimbe patirūpake. Pabhāyaṃ āloke.

Paṭibimba: in the sense of a likeness or reflection. Prabhā: in the sense of light or radiance.

955. Ghammo nidāgho cāti dve abhidhānāni. Sedajale kāyato mutte.

955. Ghamma and nidāgha are two terms for the same thing. Ghamma: also in the sense of sweat released from the body.

Kantane chedane. Vikappe vitakke. Sajjane hatthādīnaṃ sajjane.

Kantana: in the sense of cutting. Vikappa: in the sense of thought. Sajjana: in the sense of preparing, such as the preparing of hands and so on.

956. Deso desaviseso. Aṅgasaddo puṃbahutte. “Bahumhī”tipi pāṭho. Aṅgasaddo bahutte desetyattho. Vapumhi sarīre aṅgaṃ. Avayave hetumhi ca aṅgaṃ.

956. Aṅga: a specific country. The word 'Aṅga' is in the masculine plural. There is also the reading 'bahumhī.' The word 'Aṅga' in the plural means 'country.' Aṅga: in the context of the body. Aṅga: also in the sense of a limb or a cause.

“Aṅgaṃ gattantikopāya-patikesva’ppadhānake;

Aṅgadesavisesamhi, aṅgā sambodhane’byaya”nti. –

'Aṅga' is used for a limb, nearness, a means, a symbol, and a subordinate part; also for the specific country of Aṅga; 'aṅgā' is an indeclinable in address.

Nānatthasaṅgahe.

In the Nānatthasaṅgaha.

Cetiyadume pūjetabbabhūte rukkhe assatthādo.

Cetiyaduma: a sacred tree that should be worshipped, such as the Assattha tree.

957. Sādhupurise [M 0.0549] sappurise. Kappane hatthādīnaṃ kappane. “Sajjane sajjanā kappanāya”nti nānatthasaṅgaho.

957. Sādhupurisa: in the sense of a good or virtuous person. Kappana: in the sense of the shaping or arrangement of hands and the like. The phrase 'sajjane sajjanā kappanāya' is from the Nānatthasaṅgaha.

Supane niddāyaṃ. Sutte ajāgarite. Viññāṇe suttassa viññāṇe citte taṃ supinavacanaṃ. Dassane ca supinaṃ.

In supana, it means sleep. In sutta (one who is asleep), it means not awake. The consciousness of one who is sleeping, the mind, is a meaning of supina. And supina also means seeing.

958. Paccakkhe sammukhe. Sannidhāne payoge, vidhāne ca. Bhiyyosaddo pahūtaratthe so pumā.

958. Paccakkha: in the sense of direct perception or face to face. Sannidhāna: in the sense of presence, application, and disposition. The word bhiyyo is used in the sense of abundance; it is masculine.

959. Visalittasare visena lepitasare diddho pumā. Litte lepitabbasāmaññe.

959. In the context of a poison-smeared arrow, that is, an arrow anointed with poison, the word diddha is used, and it is masculine. In litta (smeared), it means the general sense of that which is to be smeared.

Vāse vasane. Dhūmādisaṅkhāre gandhacuṇṇadhūmādinā abhisaṅkhāre. Sampaṭicchane paṭiggahaṇe.

In 'dwelling' (vāsa), it means 'garment' (vasana). In 'preparation of smoke and the like' (dhūmādisaṅkhāra), it means 'preparation with perfumed powder, smoke, and the like'. In 'receiving' (sampaṭicchana), it means 'acceptance' (paṭiggahaṇa).

960. Suppagabbhe vacanasūre.

960. In 'very bold' (suppagabbha), it means 'eloquent in speech'.

Madhucchiṭṭhe madane, yena dīpampi jālenti. Odanasambhave bhuttodanato patite lāmakasammate odanabindumhi.

In madhucchiṭṭha (beeswax), it means wax, with which they even light lamps. In odanasaṃbhava (what originates from rice), it means a drop of rice fallen from eaten rice, considered inferior.

961. Surabhimhi [M 0.0550] sugandhe.

961. In 'fragrant' (surabhi), it means 'sweet-smelling'.

Uppattiyaṃ uddhaṅgamane ca uggamanaṃ.

Uggamana means arising and upward movement.

962. Lūkhe samale, kakkhaḷe ca. Niṭṭhuravācāyaṃ akaṇṇasukhavacane.

962. In 'rough' (lūkha), it means 'dirty' (samala) and 'harsh' (kakkhaḷa). In 'harsh speech' (niṭṭhuravācā), it means 'words unpleasant to the ear'.

Ambuvege ambuno udakassa vege sote.

In 'surge of water' (ambuvega), it means 'the force of water' (ambuno vega) or 'a stream' (sota).

963. Tappare tappadhāne. Kavace uracchade. Vāravāṇe cammamaye yuddhālaṅkāre ca. Nimmoke sappānaṃ jiṇṇacammani.

963. In tappara (fervor), it means being devoted to that. In kavaca (armor), it means a breastplate. In vāravāṇa (leather shield), it means a leather war ornament. In nimmoka (slough), it means the old skin of snakes.

965. Padāne dāne. Sele pabbate.

965. In 'giving' (padāna), it means 'generosity' (dāna). In 'rock' (sela), it means 'mountain' (pabbata).

966. Lohe [M 0.0551] kāḷāyase satthaṃ. Sañcaye samūhe sattho. Yathā “sakaṭasattho”tyādi. Vattane pavattane.

966. The word sattha is used in the sense of metal, that is, black iron. The word sattho is used in the sense of a collection or multitude, as in 'a caravan of carts' and so forth. In vattana (turning), it means proceeding.

967. Valaye kaṭake.

967. In 'bracelet' (valaya), it means 'armlet' (kaṭaka).

968. Kaṇḍe vāṇe. Vāpimhi dīghikādikāyaṃ. Dupphasse dukkhasamphasse. Kakace kharapatte.

968. In 'arrow' (kaṇḍa), it means 'shaft' (vāṇa). In 'pond' (vāpi), it means 'long pond and so forth'. In 'difficult to touch' (dupphassa), it means 'painful to touch'. In 'saw' (kakaca), it means 'rough blade'.

969. Surāya kādambariyaṃ, yāya pītāya mattā sattā anāgamanīyavatthūsupi gacchanti. Rathaṅge cakke. Kāmupadhiādīsu catūsu upadhīsu ca upadhi, anitthī.

969. In surā (liquor), it means Kādambarī liquor, by drinking which beings become intoxicated and even go to improper places. In rathaṅga (chariot part), it means wheel. In the four attachments beginning with attachment to sensual pleasures, the word upadhi is also used, and it is not feminine.

970. Dabbe [M 0.0552] dhanādike. Bhūbhedo vatthādi. Mahārāje catūsu mahārājesu ekasmiṃ mahārāje. Nare satte.

970. In 'substance' (dabba), it means 'wealth and so forth'. 'Bhūbheda' means 'cloth and so forth'. In 'great king' (mahārāja), it means 'one of the four great kings'. In 'man' (nara), it means 'being' (satta).

971. Āpaṇe kayavikkayaṭṭhāne. Sambhāre upakaraṇe. “Ratho sīlaparikkhāro, jhānakkho cakkavīriyo”ti saṃ. ni. 5.4 ettha alaṅkāro “parikkhāro”ti vutto.

971. In āpaṇa (shop), it means a place of buying and selling. In sambhāra (requisites), it means accessories. In the phrase, 'The chariot has virtue as its equipment, jhāna as its axle, and energy as its wheel,' here embellishment is called 'equipment' (parikkhāra).

972. Vohārasmiṃ rathasakaṭādivohāre. Upaṭṭhitagirā saddato atthato ca pākaṭagirā.

972. In 'parlance' (vohāra), it means 'parlance about chariots, carts, and so forth'. 'Upaṭṭhitagirā' means 'language clear in sound and meaning'.

973. Vacanāvayaveti vākyāvayave. Hetudāharaṇādiyuttassa sambandhatthassa vacanasamūhassa avayave. Mūle lobhādike. Kāraṇe lobhādito aññasmiṃ kāraṇe. Pācānalasmiṃ udaraṭṭhe bhuttapācane kammajatejasmiṃ. Rogabhedepi gahaṇī.

973. 'Vacanāvayava' means 'part of a sentence'. It means 'a part of a collection of words whose meaning is connected and furnished with reason, example, and so forth'. In 'root' (mūla), it means 'greed and so forth'. In 'cause' (kāraṇa), it means 'a cause other than greed and so forth'. In 'digestive fire' (pācānala), it means 'the heat born of kamma that digests food in the belly'. Also, 'gahaṇī' is a type of disease.

974. Saṃyame [M 0.0553] cakkhādindriyasaṃyame.

974. In 'restraint' (saṃyama), it means 'restraint of the eye and other faculties'.

975. Muddikassa rukkhassa rase ca. Pupphassa sabbassa pupphassa rase ca. Khudde makkhikākate ca madhu punnapuṃsakaṃ.

975. Madhu means the juice of the grape-vine, and the juice of all flowers. Also, madhu (honey) made by small bees is masculine or neuter.

“Madhu khudde jale khīre, majje puppharase madhu;

Racche citte vasante ca, jīvasāke madhuddume”ti. –

'Madhu' means: in a small bee, in water, in milk, in liquor, in flower juice; and in a road, in the variegated, in spring, in the Jīvaka plant, and in the Madhuka tree.

Nānatthasaṅgahe.

In the Nānatthasaṅgaha.

Ulloceti seyyādīnaṃ uparibhāge rajopātanivāraṇatthaṃ ṭhapite dussamayādike.

'Ulloca' means 'cloths and so forth placed above beds and the like to prevent dust from falling'.

976. Apavagge nibbāne. Sudhāyaṃ devatānaṃ bhojane.

976. In 'release' (apavagga), it means 'Nibbāna'. In 'ambrosia' (sudhā), it means 'food of the devas'.

“Amataṃ yaññasesasmiṃ, pīyūse salile ghate;

Ayācite ca mokkhe ca, dhanvantarisudhāsisu;

Amato amatā sivā-gaḷo jhāmalakīsu ce”ti medinīkosa 16.77-8 gāthāyampi.

'Amata' means: in the remnants of a sacrifice, in nectar, in water, in ghee; in the unasked, in release, in Dhanvantari's nectar, in fangs; Amato (masculine), amatā (feminine), auspicious, Śiva's throat, and in Emblic myrobalan fruits.

Nānatthasaṅgahe vuttaṃ. Mohe avijjāyaṃ. Timire andhakāre. Saṅkhyā gaṇanaviseso. Guṇe tatiye guṇe.

It is stated in the Nānatthasaṅgaha. In 'delusion' (moha), it means 'ignorance' (avijjā). In 'darkness' (timira), it means 'darkness' (andhakāra). 'Saṅkhyā' means 'a specific count'. In 'quality' (guṇa), it means 'the third quality'.

977. Khare [M 0.0554] pharuse. Akāriye akattabbe. Purise pulliṅge. Sukate kusale dhamme puññaṃ paṇḍake napuṃsake. Pavane pūte.

977. In 'harsh' (khara), it means 'rough' (pharusa). In 'what should not be done' (akāriya), it means 'what should not be done' (akattabba). In 'man' (purisa), it means 'masculine gender'. In 'well-done' (sukata), it means 'in a wholesome state', 'merit', 'in a eunuch', and 'in the neuter gender'. In 'wind' (pavana), it means 'purified'.

978. Asiniddho sukkho. Saṅge lagge.

978. 'Asiniddha' means 'dry'. In 'clinging' (saṅga), it means 'attached' (lagga).

979. Lañchane paṭibimbe. Sīmā mariyādo. Pakāro tulyo.

979. In 'mark' (lañchana), it means 'reflection' (paṭibimba). 'Sīmā' means 'boundary' (mariyāda). 'Pakāra' means 'similar' (tulya).

980. Mantane catukkaṇṇādike. Byasane bhogabyasanādike. Vipattiyaṃ anatthe.

980. In 'deliberation' (mantana), it means 'a secret conversation and so forth'. In 'disaster' (byasana), it means 'disaster of possessions and so forth'. In 'calamity' (vipatti), it means 'misfortune' (anattha).

981. Raṃsibhedo [M 0.0555] pubbe udayato sūriyassa raṃsiviseso. Abyattarāge kiñciratte. Lohite ratte.

981. 'Raṃsibheda' means 'a special ray of the sun from its rising in the east'. In 'slight passion' (abyattarāga), it means 'somewhat reddened'. In 'red' (lohita), it means 'reddened' (ratta).

Pakatānivatte pakatito anivattane. “Pakatiyañca anivattane cā”tipi attho. Nassanakkhareti vināsanakkhare. Nassa adassane akkhare.

In 'not turning back from the natural state' (pakatānivatta), it means 'not turning back from the natural state'. The meaning is also 'in the natural state and in not turning back'. 'Nassanakkhara' means 'destructive letters'. 'Nassa' means 'in disappearance', 'in invisible letters'.

“Anubandho pakatyādo, dosuppāde vinassare;

Susumukhyānusāresu, pakatassā’nuvattane”ti amara 23.98 gāthāyampi passitabbaṃ. –

The word 'anubandha' is used in the sense of: 'the natural state and so forth', 'the arising of faults', 'what is perishable', 'in the Susumukhyā and related treatises', and 'the continuation of the natural state'.

Nānatthasaṅgahe.

From the Nānatthasaṅgaha.

982. Avataraṇe otaraṇe. Titthasmiṃ nadyādīnaṃ titthe. Vivare vivaraṇe. Iṅgite sīsacalanādike.

982. In 'descending' (avataraṇa), it means 'alighting' (otaraṇa). In 'ford' (tittha), it means 'a ford of rivers and so forth'. In 'opening' (vivara), it means 'creating an opening' (vivaraṇa). In 'sign' (iṅgita), it means 'movement of the head and so forth'.

983. Khattā khattiyato sañjāte sudditthitanaye sudditthiyā putte ca. Tibbamhi adhimatte ca. So uggo. Aggo seṭṭho. Dhiti vīriyaṃ.

983. 'Khattā' means 'born of a khattiya', and 'a son of a well-established woman'. In 'intense' (tibba), it means 'excessive'. 'Ugga' means 'fierce'. 'Agga' means 'foremost'. 'Dhiti' means 'energy'.

984. Pabhāte paccūse. Niroge rogamutte. Sajje saṅgate, ādhārepi ca. “Sajjutto sannaddhe saṅgatepi ce”ti nānatthasaṅgahe. Dakkho cheko. Yuttepi kallaṃ. Kūṭacariyāyaṃ saṭhacariyāyaṃ.

984. In 'dawn' (pabhāta), it means 'early morning' (paccūsa). In 'free from disease' (niroga), it means 'released from illness' (rogamutta). In 'ready' (sajja), it means 'assembled' (saṅgata), and also 'in a receptacle' (ādhāra). As stated in the Nānatthasaṅgaha: 'Sajjutta' means 'equipped' and also 'assembled'. 'Dakkha' means 'clever'. 'Kalla' also means 'suitable'. In 'deceitful conduct' (kūṭacariya), it means 'fraudulent conduct' (saṭhacariya).

985. Pakkhibhedo pārāvatappamāṇo pakkhī. Yasmiṃ gehe palinā patite asubhanimittaṃ karonti. Pārāvate kalarave.

985. A species of bird, a bird the size of a pigeon; when it has fallen in a house, they take it as an inauspicious omen. In 'pigeon' (pārāvata), it means 'a cooing sound' (kalarava).

Saradabbhūte saradakāle sambhūte. Appagabbhe kātaravacane.

In 'born in autumn' (saradabbhūta), it means 'come into being in the autumn season'. In 'modest' (appagabbha), it means 'with timid speech' (kātaravacana).

986. Kaṭhine kakkhaḷe. Sāhaso balakkāro. Appiye amanāpe. Cīre nantake, vāke ca cīraṃ.

986. In 'hard' (kaṭhina), it means 'rough' (kakkhaḷa). 'Sāhasa' means 'violence' (balakkāra). In 'unpleasant' (appiya), it means 'disagreeable' (amanāpa). 'Cīra' means 'bark-cloth' (nantaka), and 'cīraṃ' also means 'bark' (vāka).

987. Migabhede [M 0.0557] kukkurappamāṇe mige. Paṭākāyaṃ dhaje. Mocaṃ pasiddhaṃ, kadalī īkāranto. Dakkhiṇā kammaphalaṃ saddahitvā dātabbaṃ dānaṃ.

987. In 'a species of deer' (migabheda), it means 'a deer the size of a dog'. In 'banner' (paṭākā), it means 'flag' (dhaja). 'Moca' is well-known; 'kadalī' ends in ī. 'Dakkhiṇā' means 'a gift to be given with faith in the fruit of action'.

988. Uppāte bhūtavikatiyaṃ. Vessānare aggimhi.

988. In 'portent' (uppāta), it means 'an abnormality of beings' (bhūtavikati). In 'Vessānara', it means 'fire' (aggi).

989. Potavāhe talakavāhe. Niyantari pājitari.

989. In 'sailor' (potavāha), it means 'raft-bearer' (talakavāha). In 'controller' (niyantari), it means 'driver' (pājitari).

990. Rodhane āvaraṇe.

990. In 'obstructing' (rodhana), it means 'hindering' (āvaraṇa).

991. Bhājane vilīvamayādike. Pariyatti pariyāpuṇanaṃ sikkhanaṃ, pariyāpuṇitabbā vā sikkhitabbā. Jarāsithilacammasmiṃ jarāya kāraṇabhūtāya sithilacammani. Udaraṅge udaracammarājiyaṃ.

991. In 'vessel' (bhājana), it means 'made of basket-work and so forth'. 'Pariyatti' means 'learning' or 'training', or 'what should be learned' or 'what should be trained'. In 'aged, loose skin' (jarāsithilacamma), it means 'loose skin caused by old age'. In 'abdominal part' (udaraṅga), it means 'a line on the abdominal skin' (udaracammarāji).

992. Vidāritādīsu [M 0.0558] tīsupi vāccaliṅgikaṃ. Upajāpe catutthopāye.

992. In 'splitting' and so forth, in all three, it is to be understood as feminine gender. In 'sowing dissension' (upajāpa), it means 'the fourth stratagem'.

993. Gāmasandohe gāmasamūhe. Paridhi pariveso sūriyādigehaṃ. Āgame buddhavacane. Lekhe vācitalekhe.

993. In 'collection of villages' (gāmasandoha), it means 'a group of villages' (gāmasamūha). 'Paridhi' means 'halo' (parivesa) or 'the abode of the sun and so forth'. In 'Āgama', it means 'the word of the Buddha' (buddhavacana). In 'writing' (lekha), it means 'a written letter' (vācitalekha).

994. Ayomayavijjhanakaṇṭako sūjhādivijjhanaṃ. Guṇukkaṃse guṇātisaye. Vibhave bhoge. Sampatti, sampadāti ca abhidhānadvayaṃ.

994. 'An iron piercing-thorn' (ayomayavijjhanakaṇṭaka) means 'piercing with a needle and so forth' (sūcyādivijjhana). In 'excellence of qualities' (guṇukkaṃsa), it means 'superiority of qualities' (guṇātisaya). In 'wealth' (vibhava), it means 'possessions' (bhoga). 'Sampatti' and 'sampadā' are two terms.

995. Bhū pathavī. Yogyādīsu tīsvatthesu tīsu. Yogye anucchavike. Yutte saṅgate. Addho addhasaddo bhāge samabhāge, asamabhāge ca. Tatra same addhaṃ. Itaratra [M 0.0559] addho addhampi, pathe magge addhā pume. Kālepi addhā pume. Ekaṃse nicchaye. Caturambaṇe karīsaṃ vuttaṃ.

995. 'Bhū' means 'earth' (pathavī). In 'suitability' and so forth, in three meanings. In 'suitable' (yogya), it means 'appropriate' (anucchavika). In 'joined' (yutta), it means 'connected' (saṅgata). The word 'addha' is used for 'portion', both 'equal portion' and 'unequal portion'. Therein, for an equal portion, it is 'addhaṃ'. In other cases, it is 'addho' or 'addhampi'; for a path or road, 'addhā' is masculine. For time also, 'addhā' is masculine. In 'one aspect' (ekaṃsa), it means 'certainty' (nicchaya). A 'karīsa' is said to be four ambaṇas.

996. Usabhe gavasatajeṭṭhake gave. Seṭṭhesu ca usabho. Vīsayaṭṭhiyaṃ usabhaṃ. Tanti buddhavacanaṃ. Panti āḷi.

996. In 'bull' (usabha), it means 'the chief bull of a hundred cows'. And among the best, it is 'usabha'. In 'a measure of twenty yaṭṭhis' (vīsayaṭṭhi), it is 'usabhaṃ'. 'Tanti' means 'the word of the Buddha'. 'Panti' means 'row' (āḷi).

997. Itthinimitte itthiyā aṅgajāte. Kilañje vilīvamaye. So kaṭasaddo kate tīsu.

997. In 'female sign' (itthinimitta), it means 'the female sexual organ' (itthiyā aṅgajāta). In 'mat' (kilañja), it means 'made of basket-work' (vilīvamaya). The word 'kaṭa' is used in three senses.

“Kaṭo soṇikriyākāre,

Kilañje’tisaye sive;

Samaye gajagaṇḍe ca,

Kaṭā vippaliyaṃ matā”ti medinīkosa 11.3. –

'Kaṭa' is used in the sense of 'the manner of making a sound', 'a mat' (kilañja), 'excellence' (atisaya), 'the auspicious' (siva), 'time' (samaya), and 'an elephant's temple' (gajagaṇḍa). 'Kaṭā' is considered a variant.

Vopālito. “Samaye ca kriyākāre, kilañje ca sare kaṭo”ti tikaṇḍaseso tikaṇḍasesa 3.3.93. Mandirālindavatthuni gehassa ālindabhāge vatthumhi.

Vopālita. As stated in the Tikaṇḍaśeṣa: 'Kaṭa' is used in the sense of 'time', 'action', 'a mat' (kilañja), and 'sound'. 'Mandirālindavatthu' means 'the foundation site of a house's porch'.

998. Mathite gorasavisese. Sūciphale ambilapattaphale. Duddasetare passituṃ adukkare.

998. In 'churned' (mathita), it means 'a special kind of milk product' (gorasavisesa). In 'needle-fruit' (sūciphala), it means 'a fruit with sour leaves' (ambilapattaphala). In 'other than hard to see' (duddasetara), it means 'not difficult to see' (passituṃ adukkara).

999. Antarīpaṃ [M 0.0560] jalamajjhathalaṃ. Pajjoto padīpo. Bandho sambandho. Mihite īsaṃhasite.

999. 'Antarīpa' means 'a place in the middle of water' (jalamajjhathala). 'Pajjota' means 'lamp' (padīpa). 'Bandha' means 'connection' (sambandha). In 'smile' (mihita), it means 'a slight smile' (īsaṃhasita).

1000. Thiyaṃ itthisāmaññe. Itthiliṅgeti vā attho. Dāre bhariyāyaṃ. Sure devatāyaṃ, devatāvisese vā. Vāsudeve nārāyane. Antake vasavattini. Asite kāḷavaṇṇe.

1000. In 'woman' (thī), it means 'in the general sense of woman'. Or the meaning is 'feminine gender'. In 'wife' (dāra), it means 'wife' (bhariyā). In 'deity' (sura), it means 'deity', or 'a specific deity'. In 'Vāsudeva', it means 'Nārāyaṇa'. In 'destroyer' (antaka), it means 'Vasavattin'. In 'black' (asita), it means 'black color'.

1001. Upaṭṭhāne pāricariyāyaṃ, sevane ca. Aññaropane abhaṃsabhāvassa aññassa taṃsabhāvaropane. Sakko sakkasaddo. Inde devarāje sakko. Janapade sakkā. Sākiye ca khame tīsu.

1001. In 'attendance' (upaṭṭhāna), it means 'service' and 'waiting upon'. In 'imputation of otherness' (aññaropaṇa), it means 'imputation of the state of otherness to that which is not of a deviating nature'. The word is sakka. In the sense of Indra, king of the devas, it is sakko. In the sense of country, it is sakkā. And in the senses of Sākiya and capable, it is in three genders.

1002. Vajjanatthādīsu tīsu parihāro. Pañhavissajjanepi parihāro. Dvije brāhmaṇe. Vessepi ariyo.

1002. In three senses, such as the meaning of avoidance, the word is parihāra. Also, parihāra means 'answering a question'. In 'twice-born' (dvija), it means 'brahmin'. Also in 'Vessa', it means 'noble' (ariya).

1003. Suṃsumāre [M 0.0561] nakke. Ulūpini caṇḍamacchavisese. Uddālapādape selurukkhe, yassa phalāni atipicchalāni.

1003. In 'Suṃsumāra', it means 'crocodile' (nakka). In 'Ulūpinī', it means 'a kind of fierce fish'. In 'Uddālapādapa', it means 'Selu tree', whose fruits are very slippery.

1004. Piyake pītasāle. Kaṇḍe sare. Khipane asanaṃ. Asu khepane. Yuge rathayugādo. Vikāro vikati. Antike samīpe.

1004. In 'Piyaka', it means 'yellow Sāl tree'. In 'kaṇḍa', it means 'arrow'. In 'throwing' (khipana), it means 'throwing' (asana). The root asu means 'in throwing'. In 'yoke' (yuga), it means 'chariot yoke and so forth'. 'Vikāra' means 'alteration' (vikati). In 'near' (antika), it means 'close' (samīpa).

1005. Lavitte dātte. Ajjhesanā sakkārapubbikā āyācanā.

1005. In 'reaped' (lavitta), it means 'sickle' (dātta). 'Ajjhesanā' means 'a request preceded by honor'.

1006. Makacivatthe yaṃ loke “cakkū”ti vuccati, “sāṇavattha”ntipi eke. Ganthe saddasatthādike. Lepyādikammani cittakārādīhi katarūpe.

1006. In 'Makacivattha', it is what is called 'cakkū' in the world; some also call it 'sāṇavattha'. In 'text' (gantha), it means 'grammar and so forth'. In 'plastering and other work' (lepyādikamma), it means 'forms of work done by painters and so forth'.

1007. Puññavati [M 0.0562] puggale. Bhūsaṇhakaraṇiyaṃ sudhālepakānaṃ dārumayahatthe.

1007. In 'meritorious' (puññavat), it means 'person'. 'Bhūsaṇhakaraṇiya' means 'a wooden tool of plasterers for applying stucco'.

1008. Pāyite pātabbe, “vāyite”tipi pāṭho. “Dayite”tipi kvaci dissati.

1008. In 'caused to drink' (pāyita), it means 'drinkable' (pātabba); 'vāyita' is also a reading. 'Dayita' is also seen in some places.

1009. Lohitādimhi vaṇṇavisese. Rañjane “mukharāgo”tyādīsu. Pavuddhadariyaṃ mahādariyaṃ.

1009. In 'red and so forth', it means 'a specific color'. In 'dyeing' (rañjana), as in 'color of the face' and so forth. 'Pavuddhadariya' means 'a great torrent'.

1010. Kaserussa phale sakaṇṭakassa phale. Maggasamāgame caccare. Bahulāyaṃ “phālātī”iti khyāte. Dose tu eḷamīritaṃ.

1010. In 'fruit of kaseru', it means 'fruit of a thorny plant'. In 'meeting of roads' (maggasamāgama), it means 'crossroads' (caccara). In 'Bahulā', it is known as 'phālātī'. But in 'fault' (dosa), it is said to be 'eḷa'.

1011. Adhikaraṇe [M 0.0563] adhikaraṇakārake. Pattādhāro bhājanassa ādhāro. Ālavālake tarusekatthaṃ tarumūlavicite sobbhajalādhāre. Agabhedo rukkhabhedo, so ca mahāsattena temiyarājakumārakāle bhuttarukkho. Tatra kārā itthī. Kāropi sakkāre, dvīsu. Bandhanālaye pana kārāyeva.

1011. In 'dispute' (adhikaraṇa), it means 'one who makes a dispute' (adhikaraṇakāraka). A 'bowl-stand' (pattādhāra) is a support for a bowl. In 'basin' (ālavālaka), it means a water-basin arranged at the root of a tree for watering the tree. 'A species of tree' (agabheda) is a type of tree, and that was the tree eaten by the Great Being during the time of Prince Temiya. There, kārā means a woman. Kāro also means honor, and is in two genders. But in the sense of a prison, it is only kārā.

1012. Meghapāsāṇe ghanopale. Kuṇḍikāyaṃ bhiṅgāre. Padātismiṃ catutthasenaṅge.

1012. In 'hailstone' (meghapāsāṇa), it means 'dense stone' (ghanopala). In 'water pot' (kuṇḍikā), it means 'pitcher' (bhiṅgāra). In 'infantry' (padāti), it means 'the fourth division of the army'.

1013. Chiddādīni tīṇi abhidhānāni susire ca dūsane aparādhe ca tīsu siyuṃ. Muccite muccitabbe.

1013. The three terms beginning with 'chidda' occur in three senses: in a hole, in a fault, and in an offense. In 'released' (muccita), it means 'to be released' (muccitabba).

1014. Hatthiliṅge hatthisaṇṭhānasakuṇe. Made nāgamade.

1014. In 'elephant-shaped' (hatthiliṅga), it means 'a bird shaped like an elephant'. In 'intoxication' (mada), it means 'elephant intoxication' (nāgamada).

1015. Atthaṅgame [M 0.0564] vināse. Nigamubbhūte nigamesañjātavatthumhi. Āpaṇopajīvini āpaṇena jīvitavuttiyaṃ kattari.

1015. In 'setting' (atthaṅgama), it means 'destruction' (vināsa). In 'that which has arisen from a town' (nigamubbhūta), it means 'a thing produced in a town'. In 'one who lives by a shop' (āpaṇopajīvin), it means 'an agent whose livelihood is by a shop'.

1016. Haritasmiṃ sukapattavaṇṇe. Paṇṇe chadamatte.

1016. In 'green' (harita), it means 'the color of a parrot's wing'. In 'leaf' (paṇṇa), it means 'a mere covering'.

1017. Phalamhi rukkhādīnaṃ phalamatte. Taṃ pakkavacanaṃ. Nāsamukhe nāsābhimukhe ca pariṇate ca tīsu.

1017. In 'fruit' (phala), it means merely the fruit of trees and so on. That is a mature expression. In the senses of 'tip of the nose', 'facing the nose', and 'ripened', it is in three genders.

Ājīvane jīvitavuttiyaṃ. Piṇḍane rāsikaraṇe. Goḷake vaṭṭale.

In 'livelihood' (ājīvana), it means 'mode of living' (jīvitavutti). In 'collecting' (piṇḍana), it means 'accumulating' (rāsikaraṇa). In 'ball' (goḷaka), it means 'sphere' (vaṭṭala).

1018. Paribbaye vetane. Kammādike kammavaṭṭavipākavaṭṭakilesavaṭṭe. Vaṭṭale bubbuḷasaṇṭhāne. Paccāhāre paṭivacanāhāre.

1018. In 'expenditure' (paribbaya), it means 'wages' (vetana). In 'cycle of kamma, etc.' (kammādika), it means 'the cycle of kamma, the cycle of result, and the cycle of defilements'. In 'sphere' (vaṭṭala), it means 'shaped like a bubble'. In 'withdrawal' (paccāhāra), it means 'retraction of speech' (paṭivacanāhāra).

1019. Vikate [M 0.0565] vikatiyaṃ, virūpe vā.

1019. In 'altered' (vikata), it means 'alteration' (vikati), or 'deformed' (virūpa).

1020. Sabyamhi adakkhiṇe. Cāru manuññaṃ. Sarabye sarena vijjhitabbe phalakādo. Cihane lakkhaṇe.

1020. In 'left' (sabya), it means 'not right' (adakkhiṇa). 'Charming' (cāru) means 'delightful' (manuñña). In 'to be pierced by an arrow' (sarabya), it means 'a target and so on, which is to be pierced by an arrow'. In 'sign' (cihana), it means 'characteristic' (lakkhaṇa).

1021. Samasippīnaṃ samānasippīnaṃ gaṇe seṇī itthī. Āvaḷiyaṃ pantiyaṃ. Sudhāyaṃ lepe. Dhūliyaṃ rajasi. Vāsacuṇṇake vāsayoggacuṇṇe.

1021. In the sense of a group of artisans with the same craft, the word is seṇī (guild), which is feminine. In 'row' (āvaḷi), it means 'line' (panti). In 'plaster' (sudhā), it means 'coating' (lepa). In 'dust' (dhūli), it means 'dirt' (raja). In 'perfumed powder' (vāsacuṇṇaka), it means 'powder suitable for perfuming'.

1022. Atipasatthe pasatthassa jo, ativuḍḍhe vuḍḍhassa. Takke gorasavisese. Hotīti kriyāpadaṃ.

1022. In the sense of 'most praised', it is the superlative of 'praised'; in the sense of 'very old', it is the superlative of 'old'. In 'buttermilk' (takka), it means 'a special kind of milk product'. The word 'hoti' is a verb.

1023. Paṇe jūtakārādīnaṃ kammani. Kaṇhe kāḷe.

1023. In 'wager' (paṇa), it means 'the action of gamblers and so on'. In 'black' (kaṇha), it means 'dark' (kāḷa).

1024. Sambhave [M 0.0566] sukke. Amejjhe apavitte.

1024. In 'origin' (sambhava), it means 'semen' (sukka). In 'impure' (amejjha), it means 'unholy' (apavitta).

1025. Ikke bahulome kāḷamige. Baḷise macchavedhane. Selabhede vaṅkanāmake pabbate.

1025. In 'Ikka deer' (ikka), it means 'a black deer with much hair'. In 'fish-hook' (baḷisa), it means 'fish-piercer' (macchavedhana). In 'a type of rock' (selabheda), it means 'the mountain named Vaṅka'.

1026. Kuṇapamhi matakāye. Addhamhi samaddhabhāge, tenāha “purise”ti, “purise”ti ca yebhuyyappavattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tenāha “vā khaṇḍaṃ sakalaṃ pume”ti.

1026. In 'corpse' (kuṇapa), it means 'dead body'. In 'half' (addha), it means 'a complete half-portion'. Therefore, it is said 'in a man', and 'in a man' is said with reference to its general prevalence; therefore, it is said 'or a fragment, or the whole, in the masculine gender'.

1027. Saṃvarīmukhe rattiyā ādimhi.

1027. In 'the face of Saṃvarī' (saṃvarīmukha), it means 'at the beginning of the night'.

1030. Devabhedo [M 0.0567] kumbhaṇḍo nāma yakkho. Vallijātiyaṃ yassā phalāni ukkhalippamāṇāni honti. Catutthaṃse catutthabhūte koṭṭhāse. Pade caraṇe. Paccantasele pabbatapāde.

1030. 'A type of deity' (devabheda) is a yakkha named Kumbhaṇḍa. In 'a type of creeper' (vallijāti), it means one whose fruits are the size of cooking pots. In 'fourth part' (catutthaṃsa), it means 'the fourth division'. In 'foot' (pada), it means 'step' (caraṇa). In 'border mountain' (paccantasela), it means 'foot of a mountain' (pabbatapāda).

1031. Lohantare setalohe. Bahumhi bahuvacane. Kammārabhaṇḍabhede “tū”iti khyāte. Khaṭake kuñcikapāṇimhi.

1031. In another metal, in white metal. In many, in the plural. In a type of blacksmith's tool known as 'tū'. In a cot, in one holding a key in hand.

1032. Doṇiyaṃ kaṭṭhamaye dhaññamānike. Adhiṭṭhitiyaṃ upariṭṭhāne. Ṭhāne ṭhānamatte.

1032. In a trough, in a wooden grain measure. In a determination, in a superior position. In a place, merely a place.

1034. Koṭṭhāsabhedasmiṃ [M 0.0568] “vakkaṃ hadaya”ntyādīsu ma. ni. 1.110. Vaṅke kuṭilye. Dibbacakkhupubbenivāsānussatiāsavakkhayasaṅkhātā tisso vijjā, ādinā aṭṭha vijjā gahitā. Buddhiyaṃ ñāṇe.

1034. In the division of parts, such as 'kidneys, heart' and so on. In the crooked, in crookedness. The three knowledges, namely the divine eye, recollection of past lives, and the destruction of the taints; by 'and so on,' eight knowledges are included. In intellect, in knowledge.

1035. Anākule ākularahite. Siloke anuṭṭhubhādo. Addhe bhāge. Tīsu pajjo pajjasaddo.

1035. In the undisturbed, free from disturbance. In a verse, the anuṭṭhubha meter and so on. In half, in a part. In three senses, the word for verse is 'pajja'.

1036. Rukkhabhedasmiṃ udakappasādanaphale. Kittime karaṇena nipphatte. Vidheyye vacanaggāhini. Pubbamhi pūye.

1036. In a type of tree, in a fruit that clarifies water. In the artificial, produced by making. In the obedient, receptive to words. In pus, in pus.

1037. Laddhattharakkhaṇe [M 0.0569] laddhassa dhanādikassa atthassa rakkhaṇe. Niyojane pesane. Kāriye phale.

1037. In protecting what has been gained, in protecting wealth and other acquired possessions. In employing, in dispatching. In the effect, in the result.

1038. Assāsappatte laddhassāse. Bodhidume amhākaṃ bhagavato bodhirukkhe. Kurūre kakkhaḷakārake. Nesādamhi migamacchādiludde.

1038. In one who has attained ease, in one who has gained confidence. In the Bodhi tree, the enlightenment tree of our Blessed One. In the cruel, in that which causes harshness. In a hunter, in one who is cruel to deer, fish, and so on.

1039. Laggasmiṃ saṅge. Majjhamhi udare. Bhāge asamaddhabhāge. Dhanimhi mahaddhane.

1039. In attachment, in clinging. In the middle, in the belly. In a part, in an incomplete part. In the wealthy, in one with great wealth.

1040. Gahane saṅkare. Sasantāne attano niyakajjhattasantāne. Visayagocarānaṃ viseso vutto.

1040. In a thicket, in a tangle. In one's own continuity, in one's own personal inner continuity. The distinction between sense-objects and their ranges is stated.

Gāthāddhavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the half-verses is finished.

1041. Bhuvane [M 0.0570] kāmabhavādike. Jane pāṇimhi. Yase kittiyaṃ. Pajje anuṭṭhubhādo. Rukkhe rukkhabhede.

1041. In the world, in the sensual realm and so on. In a person, in a living being. In fame, in renown. In a verse, the anuṭṭhubha meter and so on. In a tree, in a type of tree.

1042. Vaṭo vaṭarukkho. Vāyase kāke. Bake setapatte. Avasaro avakāso. Ahaṃ dinaṃ. Kuce nārithane. Abbhe meghe.

1042. A banyan, a banyan tree. In a crow, in a crow. In a heron, in a white-winged bird. Opportunity, occasion. A day, a day. In a breast, in a woman's breast. In a cloud, in a cloud.

1043. Ucchaṅge pallaṅkoparibhāge. Lakkhaṇe ñāpake.

1043. In the lap, in the upper part of a couch. In a characteristic, in an indicator.

Diṭṭhobhāsesu dassane, obhāse cāti atthesu.

In the seen and in splendor, that is, in the meanings of 'seeing' and 'splendor'.

1044. Sūraṃsūsu sūriye, kiraṇe ca. Dame damane. Mānaṃ mānaviseso. Sānu pabbatasānu.

1044. Regarding 'sūra' and 'aṃsu': in the sun and in a ray. In taming, in taming. Pride, a special kind of pride. A ridge, a mountain ridge.

1045. Tāpo [M 0.0571] sūriyasantāpo. Sapace caṇḍāle, saṃ sunakhaṃ pacatīti sapaco. Pasu catuppado. Kuruṅgo ajinayoni. Ulūko koṭarasakuṇo. Indo sakko. “Mahinde guggululūka-palaggāhesu kosiyo”ti amarasīho.

1045. Heat, the sun's heat. In a dog-cooker, in an outcaste; 'he cooks a dog,' thus he is a dog-cooker. An animal, a four-footed one. A kuruṅga deer, one whose origin is hide. An owl, a hollow-dwelling bird. Indra, Sakka. Amarasimha says: 'The word Kosiya is used for Mahinda, guggulu, ulūka, and palaggāha'.

1046. Māṇavo macco. Attā sarīrādhipatidevatā. Sire uttamaṅge. Tipumhi kāḷalohe.

1046. A young man, a mortal. Self, the presiding deity of the body. In the head, in the uppermost part. In tin, in black metal.

1047. Bali bhāgadeyyo. Hattho pāṇi. Aṃsu bhā. Dante rade. Vippe brāhmaṇe. Aṇḍaje aṇḍasañjāte. Pajje anuṭṭhubhādo. Ānanaṃ mukhaṃ. Ācāro asītimahāvattādi. Dhaññaṅge bhinnataṇḍule. Sukhume aṇumhi. “Lavalesakaṇāṇavo”ti hi amarasīhena sukhumapariyāyo kaṇo vutto.

1047. Tribute, a share to be given. Hand, hand. Ray, light. In a tooth, in a tusk. In a Brahmin, in a Brahmin. In an egg-born, in that which is born from an egg. In a verse, the anuṭṭhubha meter and so on. Face, mouth. Conduct, the eighty great duties and so on. In a grain particle, in broken rice. In the subtle, in an atom. Amarasimha has stated that 'kaṇa' is a synonym for the subtle, with the verse: 'Lava, lesa, kaṇa, aṇu'.

1048. Thūṇā [M 0.0572] gehādīnaṃ padhānadāru. Jaḷattaṃ mūḷhattaṃ. Kummāso māsavikati. Byañjanaṃ tadaññabyañjanaṃ. Phoṭo nāma yasmiṃ pūye viparīte dukkhavedanā natthi. Kapolo nāma mukhacūḷikānaṃ antaraṭṭhānaṃ. Mūlye mūladhane.

1048. A pillar, the main timber of a house and so on. Dullness, stupidity. Kummāsa, a product of beans. Sauce, a different kind of sauce. A blister is that in which there is no painful sensation even when it becomes purulent. A cheek is the space between the corners of the mouth. In value, in capital.

1049. Bhāsapakkhī ca pakkhī ca bhāsapakkhino, tesu, “sakunto pakkhibhedepi, bhāsapakkhi vihaṅgame”ti hi “bhāsantaṃ sundarākāre, bhāsanto bhāsapakkhinī”ti ca vopālito. “Sakunto bhāsapakkhinī”tipi pāṭho. Bhāgye subhāsubhāvahe kammani. Vidhāne karaṇe.

1049. Regarding 'bhāsapakkhin' and 'pakkhin', which are types of birds: Vopālita says, 'A sakunta is a type of pakkhin, while a bhāsapakkhin is a vihaṅgama,' and also, 'From speaking beautifully, it is a bhāsapakkhin.' There is also the reading, 'A sakunta is a bhāsapakkhin.' In fortune, in kamma that brings good and bad results. In arrangement, in making.

1050. Yo ākāsaṃ abbhuggantvā puna otaritvā udakabbhantare macche gaṇhāti, so nīlasakuṇo cātako nāma. Eṇe eṇīmigakhyāte. Saro kaṇḍo. Sede sedane, sida pāke. Pāko pacanaṃ. Bhikkhubhede “gaṇapūrako”tyādīsu. Caye samūhe.

1050. The one who, having risen into the sky and descended again, catches fish within the water, that blue bird is named Cātaka. In an eṇa deer, known as the black antelope. An arrow, a shaft. In sweat, in sweating; the root 'sid' is in the sense of 'cooking'. Cooking, the act of cooking. In types of monks, such as 'one who completes the quorum' and so on. In a heap, in a collection.

1051. Puñje [M 0.0573] piṇḍe. Meso usabho methunaṃ kakkaṭo sīho kaññā tulā vicchiko dhanu makaro kumbho mīnoti mesādi. Loṇe lavaṇuttame. Saṃvaṭṭe vināsakappe. Kamuke tambūlaphalarukkhe.

1051. In a heap, in a mass. Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces—these are the signs beginning with Aries. In salt, in excellent salt. In the dissolution, in the eon of destruction. In the areca palm, the tree bearing the betel nut.

1052. Amate devatābhojane. Lepe suddhasakkharacuṇṇādimaye. Satthe dīghadaṇḍe satthavisese. Najjantareti gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahīti pañcasu mahānadīsu pañcamāya mahānadiyaṃ. Bhuvi pathaviyaṃ. Kriyā nārīsiṅgārabhāvajā kriyā. Vilāso pana tadaññajo. Atraje putte.

1052. In ambrosia, in food for deities. In a paste, made of pure sugar powder and so on. In a weapon, in a special weapon with a long handle. 'Between the rivers' refers to the fifth of the five great rivers, namely the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī. On the earth, on the ground. Action, an action arising from the state of feminine adornment. Grace, however, arises from something else. In a son, in a son.

1053. Kutho hatthipiṭṭhattharaṇaṃ. Veṇī nārīnaṃ kesakalāpo. “Paveṇī veṇī kuthayo”ti hi vopālito. “Paveṇī kulaveṇīsū”tipi kvaci pāṭho. Vutti bhavanaṃ[M 0.0574]. Vuttā vuttanto. Vetane kammena laddhabbe. Bharaṇe posane, dhāraṇe ca.

1053. A kutha, an elephant's back-covering. A braid, a woman's tress of hair. Vopālita says: 'Paveṇī, veṇī, kuthayo'. 'Paveṇī kulaveṇīsū' is also a reading in some places. Existence, dwelling. Spoken, a report. In wages, in what is to be obtained by work. In maintaining, in nourishing, and in supporting.

1054. Mariyādasaddo dvīsu. Sattā vijjamānatā. Samiddhi sampatti. Soppe niddāyaṃ. Vutti jīvitavutti.

1054. The word 'mariyāda' is used in two senses. Existence, being present. Success, prosperity. In sleep, in sleep. Livelihood, mode of living.

1055. Kucchā garahā. Apavādo avaṇṇavādo, abhūtākkhānampi. Dhaññe dhaññavisese, yassa sīsaṃ aṅguṭṭhappamāṇaṃ dīghañca. Piyaṅgu gandhadabbaṃ. Mokkhe nibbāne. Sive kalyāṇe.

1055. Reproach, blame. Censure, speaking ill, and also false accusation. In grain, in a special kind of grain, whose head is thumb-sized and long. Piyaṅgu, a fragrant substance. In liberation, in Nibbāna. In the auspicious, in welfare.

1056. Rañjane kāsāyādirañjane. Sūrate methune. Vāse vasanakriyāyaṃ.

1056. In dyeing, in dyeing with saffron-colored dye and so on. In sexual intercourse, in sexual intercourse. In dwelling, in the act of dwelling.

1057. Patthe mānatumbe. Nāḷe uppalādīnaṃ nāḷe. Pipāsāyaṃ pātumicchāyaṃ. Vutti bhavanaṃ.

1057. In a pattha, in a measuring pot. In a stalk, in the stalk of a lotus and so on. In thirst, in the desire to drink. Existence, dwelling.

1058. Pāṇyaṅge [M 0.0575] saṅkhanābhiyaṃ. Cakkante cakkassa ante.

1058. In a part of the hand, in the navel of a conch. At the edge of a wheel, at the end of a wheel.

“Nābhi pāṇyaṅgaṅge khette, cakkantacakkavattisu;

Nābhi padhāne katthūri-maṃse ca kvaci kittito”ti. –

'Nābhi' is said in some places to mean: a part of the hand, a field, the edge of a wheel, and a universal monarch. 'Nābhi' is also mentioned as meaning principal, musk, and flesh.

Vopālito.

Vopālita.

1059. Antareti dvinnaṃ antare. “Vīci sukhataraṅgesū”ti vopālito. Thiratte thirabhāve. “Dhīratte”tipi pāṭho, soyevattho. Save savane.

1059. Antara means between two. Vopālita states: 'Vīci is in the waves of happiness.' In steadfastness, in stability. 'Dhīratte' is also a reading; the meaning is the same. In sound, in hearing.

1060. Nissaye ādhāre.

1060. In dependence, in support.

1061. Vitte dhane. Aṅko lakkhaṇaṃ. Buddhi ñāṇaṃ. Khe ākāse.

1061. In wealth, in riches. A mark, a sign. Intellect, knowledge. In space, in the sky.

1062. Vate [M 0.0576] titthiyasamācāre. Āgumhi aparādhe. Maṇi silāvikati, maṇisaṅkhāto vā ratanaviseso idha maṇi nāma. Hāyane saṃvacchare. Vuṭṭhi vassanaṃ.

1062. In a vow, in the conduct of sectarians. In an offense, in a transgression. Maṇi is a stone artifact, or a special kind of gem known as 'maṇi' is here called maṇi. In a year, in a year. Rain, rainfall.

1063. Lipi akārādīnaṃ sannivesaviseso. Mokkho nibbānaṃ. Rate sūrate.

1063. Script, a special arrangement of letters beginning with 'a'. Liberation, Nibbāna. In pleasure, in sexual intercourse.

1064. Pāpe ca asubhe ca riṭṭhaṃ. Ariṭṭhaṃpyatra, tabbhāve tatra akāro. Aparādho ādīnavo. Ketumhi paṭākāyaṃ. Cihane lakkhaṇe. “Dhajo soṇḍikalesesu, paṭākāyañca cihane”ti vopālito.

1064. In evil and in the inauspicious, it is 'riṭṭha'. 'Ariṭṭha' is also used here; the 'a' there indicates its absence. Offense, fault. In a banner, in a flag. In a sign, in a characteristic. Vopālita states: 'Dhaja is used in the sense of an elephant's trunk, a liquor shop, a flag, and a sign.'

1065. Dvāramattepi bahidvārepi. Ito paraṃ ye anekatthā vuccante, te vāccaliṅgā. Phuṭe pākaṭe.

1065. Even at the mere door, even at the outer door. From here on, those many-meaning words that are spoken are of variable gender. In the manifest, in the evident.

1066. Ajjhakkhe [M 0.0577] adhikate. Jaḷe aññāṇe. Lolupe atitaṇhe. Cale kampite.

1066. Ajjhakkha: in one who is appointed. Jaḷa: in ignorance. Lolupa: in excessive craving. Cala: in what is shaken.

1067. Vikate virūpe. Komalaṃ akaṭhinaṃ. Atikhiṇo kuṇṭho.

1067. In the deformed, in the misshapen. Komala: soft, not stiff. Atikhiṇa: very worn out, blunt.

1068. Site sete. Sūcako pesuññakārako. Ahi sappo. Sakke khame. “Satte”ti pāṭhe pana sattiyuttetyattho. Sambandhe avippayoge. Akhile sakale.

1068. In the white. Sūcaka: an informer, a tale-bearer. Ahi: a snake. In the able, in the enduring. But in the reading 'satte,' the meaning is 'endowed with power.' In relation, in non-separation. In the complete, in the whole.

1069. Kevalaṃ asammissaṃ. Anto avasānaṃ. Adhamo nihīno. Paṇato buddhādīsu ninno. Ninno thalapaṭipakkho.

1069. Kevala: unmixed. Anto: end. Adhama: low, base. Paṇata: inclined toward the Buddha and the like. Ninna: the opposite of dry land.

1070. Suddhe [M 0.0578] aññena asammissite. Pūte mejjhe.

1070. In the pure, in what is unmixed with another. In the pure, in the clean.

1071. Byāpe byāpite. Bhāvini anāgate vatthumhi. There jiṇṇe.

1071. In what is pervaded. Bhāvin: in a future matter. In an elder, in the aged.

1072. Bahusaddo “ekasmiṃ, dvīsu ca na pavattatī”tyādīsuyeva pavattatīti maññamāno “tyādo”ti vadati. “Ekavacanaṃ, bahuvacana”nti vuttattā pana dvīsupi bahusaddo vattateva. Ācariyena vā parasamayavacanāni manasi katvā “tyādo”ti vuttaṃ. Tividhañhi tattha vacanaṃ ekavacanaṃ dvivacanaṃ bahuvacananti. Sabbapārisadattā hi byākaraṇassa sabbesaṃ vādā katthaci kathīyante.

1072. Thinking that the word 'bahusadda' (plural) applies only in cases such as 'not in one or two,' one says 'tyādo' (etc.). However, since it is stated as 'singular, plural,' the word 'bahusadda' indeed applies even to two. Alternatively, the teacher, keeping in mind the statements of other schools, said 'tyādo.' For there the number is threefold: singular, dual, and plural. Because grammar is for all assemblies, the views of all are discussed somewhere.

Dhī vuccati paññā, sā yassa atthi, sa dhīro, budho. Dhānaṃ vā dhī, sā yassatthīti sa dhīro, dhitimanto. Dhute cale.

Dhī is called wisdom; he who has it is wise, enlightened. Or, dhī is steadfastness; he who has it is wise, resolute. In the shaken, in the moved.

1073. Yāne [M 0.0579] hatthādiyāne yoggaṃ. Khame pana yoggo.

1073. Yoggaṃ: in the sense of a vehicle, a conveyance such as an elephant. However, in the sense of enduring, 'yoggo' is used.

1074. Vuḍḍhe āyuvuḍḍhe. Kulaje kulīne. Vuddho āyuvuḍḍho. Uru pamāṇato mahanto.

1074. In the old, in one advanced in age. In the well-born, in the noble. Vuddha: advanced in age. Uru: great in measure.

1075. Vutte vattabbe. Uggate uddhaṃgate. Āditte agyādīhi, gabbite sañjātamāne.

1075. Vutta: in what is to be spoken. Uggata: in what has gone upwards. Āditta: kindled by fire and the like. Gabbita: in one with arisen pride.

1076. Vigate vigatarāge. Vāyane vīte paṭe. Bhajjite dhaññādike. Bhajja pāke.

1076. Vigata: in one devoid of passion. Vāyana: on a worn cloth. Bhajjita: in roasted grain and the like. Bhajja: in cooking.

1077. Caye [M 0.0580] samūhe. Samo tulyo. Ari sattu. “Samādisū”tipi pāṭho. Vīre akātare sūre. Ravisūroti ravisūriyo “sūro”ti vutto. Kuddhe kodhasahite. Dūsite appiye.

1077. In a heap, in a collection. Sama: equal. Ari: enemy. 'Samādisū' is also a reading. In the brave, in the undaunted, in the hero. The sun-hero, that is, the sun, is called 'hero.' In the angry, in one possessed of anger. Dūsita: in what is disliked.

1078. Arimhi sattumhi diṭṭho. Ikkhitepi diṭṭho. Pote bālake. Vate ekantasādhane vatakamme.

1078. 'Diṭṭha' is used in the sense of an enemy, a foe. 'Diṭṭha' is also used in the sense of 'seen.' In a young animal, in a child. Vata: in a vow-practice that is a sole means of accomplishment.

1079. Salākāyaṃ kusāvahāre. Dabbe varahisatiṇe. Khaye udayabbayānupassīti. Sakuṇepi vayo “visayuttannabhuttānaṃ, vayānaṃ maraṇaṃ bhave”tyādīsu. Gabbo abhimāno.

1079. Salākā: in reed-carrying. Dabba: in varahisa grass. Khaya: in observing rise and fall. Also 'vayo' is used for a bird, as in 'for birds that have eaten poisoned food, death would occur,' and so on. Gabba: pride.

1080. Biḷāle [M 0.0581] majjāre. Nakule ahisattumhi. Manthano khīramanthanadaṇḍo. Sattu taṇḍulavikatikhajjaviseso. Assādilome assādīnaṃ lome. Ghāto maraṇaṃ. Rāsi puñjo.

1080. In a cat. In a mongoose, in an enemy of snakes. Manthana: a milk-churning stick. Sattu: a special food, a preparation of parched rice. Assādiloma: in the hair of horses and the like. Ghāta: death. Rāsi: a pile.

1081. Gopagāme gopālānaṃ gāme. Rave sadde. Sārathi pājitā. Vandī thutipāṭhako.

1081. In a cowherd village, in a village of cowherds. In a sound, in a noise. Sārathi: a driver. Vandī: a reciter of praise.

“Sārathimhi ticchake ca, pasute veditepi ca;

Khattiyā brāhmaṇiyā jepi, visūto pādavandisū”ti. –

The word 'sūta' is used for a charioteer and a sharp person; for one who has given birth and one who is known; also for one born of a Khattiya woman by a Brāhmaṇa, and for bards.

Vopālito. Pupphe suttādinā asaṅkhate. Taddāme pupphadāme suttādinā saṅkhate. Sakaṭe ane. Haye asse.

Vopālita. Puppha: in flowers unstrung by thread and the like. Taddāma: in a flower garland strung by thread and the like. In a cart. In a horse.

1082. Accane pūjāyaṃ. Bhe nakkhatte. Nettamajjhe “sūlā”ti khyāte. Odhi mariyādo.

1082. Accana: in worship. Bha: in an asterism. Nettamajjha: in the eye's center, known as 'sūlā.' Odhi: a limit.

1083. Puṇṇatā [M 0.0582] paripuṇṇatā. Avajjaṃ doso. Manakkārepi ābhogo. Āḷisaddo itthī. Sakhī vayasā. Setu jalavāraṇo, nadyādimaggo ca. Satte sattiyutte, thiretyattho. “Daḷho thūle bhuse satte, pagāḷhepi daḷhe mato”ti vopālito.

1083. Puṇṇatā: completeness. Avajja: a fault. Manakkāra: also attention. The word 'āḷī' is a woman. Sakhī: a friend by age. Setu: a water barrier, and also a path over rivers and the like. Satta: possessed of power, meaning firm. Vopālita states: 'Daḷha is understood as thick, abundant, strong, and also as immersed, firm.'

1084. Mokkhe nibbāne, arahattaphalepi. Sāmini patimhi. Dhāraketi dhāretīti dhārako, tattha. Posakepi bhattā.

1084. Mokkha: in Nibbāna, and also in the fruit of arahantship. Sāmin: in a husband. Dhāraka: 'he upholds,' thus the upholder, in that sense. Bhattā: also in the sense of a nourisher.

1085. Sikhā cūḷā. Piñchaṃ pucchaṃ. Attani “saṅghikaṃ puggalika”ntyādīsu. Khepe nindāyaṃ.

1085. Sikhā: a topknot. Piñchaṃ: a tail. Attani: in oneself, as in ‘communal or personal,’ etc. Khepe: in blame.

1086. Rūpe vaṇṇe. Karīse gūthe.

1086. Rūpe: in color. Karīse: in feces.

1087. Khaṇḍe [M 0.0583] sakale. Paṇṇe rukkhādīnaṃ paṇṇe. Kaṇḍe sare. Salākā vaṇopayuttā. Sucino bhāvo sucittaṃ, tasmiṃ. Gate gamanakriyāyaṃ. “Dhāva gatisuddhiya”nti hi dhātupāṭho. Hāvo itthīnaṃ siṅgārabhāvajakriyā. Avijjāya aññāṇe. Mucchane visaññibhāve.

1087. Khaṇḍe: in a fragment. Sakale: in the whole. Paṇṇe: in the leaves of trees, etc. Kaṇḍe: in an arrow. Salākā: a surgical instrument. Sucittaṃ: the state of being pure; in that. Gate: in the act of going. ‘Dhāva gatisuddhiyaṃ’ is indeed the root text. Hāvo: a woman's action expressing amorous sentiment. Avijjāya: in unknowing. Mucchane: in a state of unconsciousness.

1088. Ghammajalaṃ kāye uṇhena sañjātajalaṃ. Pāke paccane. Goḷe “mu-yī”iti khyāte mattikāguḷake. Ucchumaye ucchurasasañjāte. Mitte piyamitte, mittamatte vā. Sahāye atthacare. Pabhū adhipati. So pulliṅgo.

1088. Ghammajalaṃ: the moisture produced by heat on the body. Pāke: in cooking. Goḷe: in a mud-ball known as ‘mu-yī.’ Ucchumaye: produced from sugarcane juice. Mitte: in a dear friend, or merely in a friend. Sahāye: in one who acts for one's welfare. Pabhū: a master. It is masculine.

1089. Kurūre kakkhaḷakammante. Parasmiṃ paraṭṭhāne, paraloke vā. Atra ṭhāne, loke vā. Aṅko cihanaṃ. Aparādhe nāṭakaparicchedepi aṅko. Apavādo lokagarahā. Dese desavisese. “Bhave janapado dese, jane janapadepi ce”ti vopālito.

1089. Kurūre: in harsh actions. Parasmiṃ: in another place, or in the other world. Atra: in this place, or in this world. Aṅko: a sign. Aṅko: also in wrongdoing, and in a scene of a play. Apavādo: worldly censure. Dese: in a specific region. Vopālita states: ‘Janapado is used for a region, and also for people.’

1090. Pajje [M 0.0584] siloke. Vacībhede byattavācāyaṃ. Anvaye santāne. Sarūpasmiṃ samānabhāve. Adhobhāge ca talaṃ.

1090. Pajje: in a verse. Vacībhede: in clear speech. Anvaye: in lineage. Sarūpasmiṃ: in the state of sameness. Talaṃ: also in the lower part.

1091. Vilagge kāyamajjhe. Vemajjhe majjhasāmaññe. Kusumaṃ pasavaṃ. Utu itthipupphaṃ. Subbate sundare vate.

1091. Vilagge: in the middle of the body. Vemajjhe: in the general middle. Kusumaṃ: a flower. Utu: a woman's menses. Subbate: in a beautiful vow.

1092. Kose liṅgapasibbake. Gabbhare guhāyaṃ. Bile kipillikādīnaṃ āvāse. Gaṇḍake khaggavisāṇe. Kadambe “thina”iti khyāte. Dume rukkhe. Caye samūhe.

1092. Kose: in the sheath of the genital organ. Gabbhare: in a cave. Bile: in the dwelling of ants and such creatures. Gaṇḍake: in a rhinoceros horn. Kadambe: known as ‘thina.’ Dume: in a tree. Caye: in a collection.

1093. Bhe nakkhattabhede. Dhenuyaṃ siṅginiyaṃ. Yoniyaṃ itthīnaṃ aṅgajāte. Sire sīse.

1093. Bhe: in a division of asterisms. Dhenuyaṃ: in a horned cow. Yoniyaṃ: in the female genital organ. Sire: in the head.

1094. Bhogīsaddo [M 0.0585] bhogavati puggale, urage ca. Sivo mahissaro. Bale thāme. Pabhāve tejasi. “Vīriyaṃ sukke pabhāve, tejo sāmatthiyesvapī”ti vopālito. Tejasaddo pana tesu ca yathāvuttesupi dvīsvatthesu, dittiyañca vattati.

1094. The word ‘bhogī’ is used for a wealthy person, and for a serpent. Sivo: the great lord. Bale: in strength. Pabhāve: in splendor. Vopālita states: ‘Vīriyaṃ is used for semen and power; tejo also for abilities.’ The word ‘teja,’ however, applies to those two meanings as mentioned, and also to radiance.

1095. Santati ādhāro. Khaggaṅge khaggassa tikhiṇāvayave. Sūte sārathimhi. Paṭihāre vacanahāre. “Vida lābhe”ti dhātvatthato vitti. Pīḷā vibādhā.

1095. Santati: a support. Khaggaṅge: in the sharp part of a sword. Sūte: in a charioteer. Paṭihāre: in a conveyor of speech. Vitti: from the meaning of the root ‘vida lābhe’ (to gain), gain. Pīḷā: affliction.

1096. Rave sadde. Palāse nittaṇḍulavīhimhi.

1096. Rave: in sound. Palāse: in rice husks without grains.

1097. Rukkhe ambaṭṭharukkhe. Parasamaye pana bādhā. Adhikappeme atisayapeme.

1097. Ambaṭṭhe: in the Ambattha tree. However, in another doctrine, it means hindrance. Adhikappeme: in excessive love.

1098. Ketumhi [M 0.0586] dhaje. Lekhye likhitabbe lekhe. Rājiyaṃ tu lekhā.

1098. Ketumhi: in a flag. Lekhye: in what is to be written, in writing. Rājiyaṃ: indeed, a line.

1099. Satthe āvudhabhede. Satte pāṇimhi. Caye samūhe.

1099. Satthe: in a kind of weapon. Satte: in a living being. Caye: in a collection.

1100. Āḷiyaṃ nadīmagge, jaladhāraṇe ca.

1100. Āḷiyaṃ: in a river's path, and in water retention.

1101. Saṃsade sabhāye. Ayanasaddo gamane, pathe ca vattati.

1101. Saṃsade: in an assembly. The word ‘ayana’ is used in the sense of going, and in the sense of path.

1102. Rukkhantare [M 0.0587] gaṇadume. Sūre sūriye. Koṇe vidisāyaṃ. Haye turaṅge ca asso. Khandhe bhujasire. Accisaddo jālāyaṃ aggijālāyaṃ. Aṃsumhi tassa, aññesañca aṃsumhi vattati. So ca no pume pulliṅge na vattati.

1102. Rukkhantare: in a group of trees. Sūre: in the sun. Koṇe: in an intermediate direction. Asso: in a horse, and in a steed. Khandhe: in the head of the arm. The word ‘acci’ is used for a flame, in a blaze of fire. Aṃsumhi: in its rays, and also in the rays of others. And it does not occur in the masculine gender.

1103. Abhāvasaddo nāse vijjamānassa nāse. Asattasaddo avijjamānatthe vattati. Bhutti bhuñjanakriyā. Pāṇe āyumhi jīvaṃ. Jane pāṇavati jīvo.

1103. The word ‘abhāva’ is used for destruction, the destruction of what exists. The word ‘asatta’ is used in the sense of non-existence. Bhutti: the act of eating. Jīvaṃ: in life-force, in life-span. Jīvo: in a person, in a living being.

1104. Chadane gahādīnaṃ chadane. Rāsi puñjo, sahadhammīnaṃ gaṇo ca.

1104. Chadane: in the covering of houses and the like. Rāsi: a pile, and also a group of fellow Dhamma-followers.

“Nikāyo nilaye lakkhye, saṃhatānaṃ samuccaye;

Ekattha bhājini vase, paramattani vuccate”ti. –

“Nikāya is said to be used for: a dwelling, a characteristic, a collection of combined things; a single place, a division, power, and the ultimate meaning.”

Vopālito. Yajane devapūjāyaṃ. Accane pūjāmatte. Dikkha muṇḍiyopanayananiyamabbatādesesu.

Vopālita. Yajane: in worship of gods. Accane: merely in worship. Dikkhā: in shaving the head, investiture, rules, vows, and instructions.

1105. Karaṇaṃ [M 0.0588] kāro, so eva kārikā, kriyā, sakatthe ṇiko. Pajjepi soyevattho. Cihane lakkhaṇe. Thīraje itthīnaṃ utumhi. Pupphe sumane. Vānare makkaṭe.

1105. Karaṇaṃ is kāra; the same is kārikā and kriyā; the suffix ṇika is used in its own sense. In a verse also, it has the same meaning. Cihane: in a characteristic. Thīraje: in women's menses. Pupphe: in a jasmine. Vānare: in a monkey.

1106. Adhare dantāvaraṇe. Kharabhe “ka-la-au”iti khyāte. Lobhapuggalepi luddho. Āvile anacche.

1106. Adhare: in a tooth-covering. Kharabhe: known as ‘ka-la-au.’ Luddho: also in a greedy person. Āvile: in what is not clear.

1107. Caramhi guttapurise.

1107. Caramhi: in a guard.

1108. Hāso ca gandho ca hāsagandhā, tesu. Gandhotra dūragāmī. Kalyāṇepi cāru. Khala calane, sañcaye ca, to, khalito.

1108. Hāsagandhā: laughter and fragrance; in those. Here, gandha is far-going. Cāru: also in what is beautiful. From the root khala, in the sense of moving and accumulating, comes khalita.

1109. Vakkale [M 0.0589] rukkhattace. Adhirohe ārohanakriyāyaṃ. Vatthantaraṃ vicittarūpaṃ vatthaṃ, yaṃ cīnadese sañjātaṃ.

1109. Vakkale: in tree bark. Adhirohe: in the act of climbing. Vatthantaraṃ: a variegated cloth, which is produced in the land of China.

1110. Paṭihāre “ḍa-gā”iti khyāte. Mukhe bhattādīnaṃ pavesanaṭṭhāne. Pete paralokaṃ gate. Aparaṇṇaṃ muggādi. Kālo tiṃsarattidivaparicchinno.

1110. Paṭihāre: in a miracle known as ‘ḍa-gā.’ Mukhe: in the place for entering food and the like. Pete: gone to the other world. Aparaṇṇaṃ: mung beans and the like. Kālo: defined by thirty nights and days.

1111. Dose kodhe. Ghāte māraṇe. Migādo catuppade. Chagale aje. Arūpe phassādike. Avhaye saññāyaṃ. Darathe kāyacittasambhūte santāpe. Bhīti bhayaṃ.

1111. Dose: in anger. Ghāte: in killing. Migādo: in a quadruped. Chagale: in a goat. Arūpe: in contact and the like. Avhaye: in perception. Darathe: in affliction arising from body and mind. Bhīti: terror.

1112. Bhāre khandhabhārādike. Sujāsaddo dabbiyaṃ kaṭacchuyaṃ, indajāyāyaṃ sakkassa bhariyāyañca. Vihāyase ākāse.

1112. Bhāre: in a burden such as the burden of the aggregates. The word ‘Sujā’ is used for a ladle, a spoon, Indra's wife, and Sakka's wife. Vihāyase: in space.

1113. Maṇike [M 0.0590] mahati udakabhājane. Ratane asmavikāre ratanasāmaññe. Selo candanapabbato. Ārāme pupphārāmādiārāme.

1113. Maṇi: in a large water vessel. Ratana: in a product of stone, in the general sense of a jewel. Sela: the sandalwood mountain. Ārāma: in a flower park and the like.

“Malayo dese selaṅgapabbatantare, malayātivutāyañcā”ti vopālito. Aṅko cihanaṃ.

Thus Vopālita: 'Malaya is used for a country, for the region between the Selaṅga mountains, and also for that which is called Atimalaya.' Aṅka: a sign.

1114. Sappimhi ghate, tadaññe hotabbe ca havi.

1114. Havi: in ghee, in clarified butter, and also in other things to be offered.

“Rahasi ca vicāre ca, viveko jaladoṇiya”nti vopālito.

Thus Vopālita: "Viveka is used for secrecy, investigation, and a water trough."

1115. Pavāhe jalappavāhe.

1115. Pavāha: in a current of water.

“Vego jave pavāhe ca, mahākālaphalepi ce”ti medinīkosa 3.24 vopālito. Khile aṇukhāṇumhi. Kaṇe appe.

Thus Vopālita: "Vego is used for swiftness, a current, and also for the great kāla-fruit." Khila: in a small post. Kaṇa: in a particle, in a small amount.

1116. Nettante [M 0.0591] cakkhukoṇe. Cittake tilake.

1116. Nettanta: at the corner of the eye. Cittaka: in a decorative mark, in a mole.

“Apāṅgaṃ aṅgahīne ca, nettante tilakepi ce”ti medinīkosa 3.28 vopālito. Muttāguṇe suttabandhamuttāyaṃ. Gahaṇaṃ gāho, tasmiṃ. Makuḷe apupphite. Rase loṇarase.

Thus Vopālita: "Apāṅga is used for one with a deficient limb, for the corner of the eye, and also for a mole." Muttāguṇa: in a string of pearls, in pearls bound by a thread. Gahaṇa: grasping; in that sense. Makuḷa: in a bud, unblossomed. Rasa: in taste, in salty taste.

1117. Ago, nago cāti dve abhidhānāni selarukkhesu vattanti. Svappe suṭṭhu appe, appataretyattho. Avadhāraṇe “namanamatta”ntyādīsu. Accane pūjāyaṃ.

1117. Aga and naga—these two terms apply to mountains and trees. Svappa: very little, exceedingly little; the meaning is 'lesser.' Avadhāraṇa: in determination, as in “namanamatta” (mere bowing), and so on. Accana: in honoring, in veneration.

1118. Chidde dose. Otaraṇaṃ jalatitthādīsu avataraṇaṃ. Ayyake pitupitari.

1118. Chidda: in a flaw, in a defect. Otaraṇa: descending into water-fords and the like. Ayyaka: in a grandfather, in the father's father.

1119. Rukkhe [M 0.0592] khaggaphale. Sune sunakhe. Gandhe adhivāsanagandhe.

1119. Khagga: in a tree, in a sword-fruit. Suna: in a dog. Gandha: in a lingering scent.

1120. Koṇe asse. Savane sote. Pantiyaṃ vīthiyaṃ. Bhāgyaṃ puññaṃ. Ekadeso tatiyabhāgādi. Ajapālake pokkhare. “Kuṭṭhaṃ roge sugandhe cā”ti vopālito.

1120. Koṇa: in a horse. Savana: in the ear. Panti: in a row, in a street. Bhāgya: merit. Ekadesa: a portion, such as a third part. Ajapālaka: in a lotus pond. Thus Vopālita: “Kuṭṭha is used for disease, and for fragrance.”

1121. Senāsane vihārādike. Sene pīṭhādike. Cundabhaṇḍamhi cundānaṃ upakaraṇe. “Bhamo’mbuniggame bhaṇḍi, cundākhye sippiyantake”ti nānatthasaṅgahe vopālito. Aṃsusaddo vatthādīnaṃ lome, kare kiraṇamatte ca. Abyaye pakārādike.

1121. Senāsana: in a dwelling, such as a monastery and the like. Sena: in a couch, such as a seat and the like. Cundabhaṇḍa: in the equipment of a turner, that is, in the tools of turners. Thus Vopālita in the Nānatthasaṅgaha: "Bhama is used for a water outlet; bhaṇḍi for a turner's tool, a craftsman's instrument." The word aṃsu refers to the nap of cloth and the like, and to a ray, a mere beam of light. As an indeclinable: for the prefix pa and so on.

1122. Khajjantare [M 0.0593] sūkaravaccasaṇṭhāne dhaññavikāre. Dise ripumhi. Pati dhavo. Ariyo adhipati.

1122. Khajjantara: in a type of food, in spoiled grain shaped like a pig's droppings. Disa: in an enemy, in a foe. Pati: a husband. Ariya: an overlord.

1123. Rāge kasāyādike rāge.

1123. Rāga: in color, such as dye and so on; and in passion.

“Raṅgo dāne khale rāge, tacche raṅgaṃ tipumhi ce”ti vopālito. Peyye udakādike. Pītiyaṃ pivanakriyāyaṃ. “Rakkhaṇe pītiyaṃ pāna”nti vopālito. Iṇe, ukkhepane ca uddhāro. Ummāre dvārummāre. Eḷakasaddassa ajassāpi vācakattā “eḷako aje”ti vuttaṃ.

Thus Vopālita: “Raṅga is used for giving, a threshing floor, passion, and carving; and raṅgaṃ for tin.” Peyya: in a drink, such as water and the like. Pīti: in delight, in the act of drinking. Thus Vopālita: “Pāna is used for protection and for delight.” Uddhāra: in debt, and in raising up. Ummāra: in a threshold, in a door threshold. Because the word 'eḷaka' also denotes a goat, it is said, “eḷaka: in a goat.”

1124. Paharaṇaṃ pahāro, pothanaṃ. Paharati etthāti pahāro, yāmo, hāyano saṃvaccharo. Kuṇḍikāyaṃ “kayā”iti khyātāyaṃ. Āḷhake catupatthappamāṇe. Bhusamhi taṇḍulattace.

1124. Paharaṇa: a blow, a striking. Pahāra: a watch of the night; also yāma, hāyana, and saṃvacchara. Kuṇḍikā: in a water pot, known as “kayā.” Āḷhaka: a measure of four patthas. Bhusa: in husk, in rice chaff.

1125. Āvāṭe [M 0.0594] kūpe. Caye samūhe ca. Kāsu sā, kāraṇe, rahasi ca upanisā.

1125. Āvāṭa: in a pit, in a well. Caya: in a heap, and in a collection. Kāsu: a pit. Upanisā: in a cause, and in secret.

“Bhave upanisā dhamme, vedantepi rahasyampī”ti vopālito. Poṭagale “pho-khā”iti khyāte. Guṇetare avajje.

Thus Vopālita: "Upanisā is used for existence, the Dhamma, the Vedanta, and also for secrecy." Poṭagala: known as “pho-khā.” Guṇetara: in what is other than a virtue, in faultlessness.

1126. Yutte “aṭṭaṃ vinicchinātī”tyādīsu. Aṭṭāle “gopuraṭṭehi saṃyutta”miccādīsu. Aṭṭite “aṭṭassaraṃkarotī”tyādīsu. Aṭṭa abhiyoge, aṭṭa atikkamahiṃsāsūti dhātvattho. Kānane vane. Uppattiyaṃ janane, vihāyasāgamane ca.

1126. In a fitting context, as in “aṭṭaṃ vinicchināti” (he decides the case), and so on. In a watchtower, as in “gopuraṭṭehi saṃyutta” (endowed with gate-towers), and so on. In one who is afflicted, as in “aṭṭassaraṃkaroti” (he makes a cry of distress), and so on. The root meaning of aṭṭa is in exertion, and also in transgression and violence. Kānana: in a forest, in a wood. Uppatti: in origination, in birth, and in moving through the sky.

1127. Lāmake nihīne. Khandhe rūpādike. Mūlaṃ mūladhanaṃ. Upadā paheṇakaṃ. Avatthāyaṃ, paṭassa ante ca dasā. Ghāto māraṇaṃ.

1127. Lāmaka: in the lowly, in the vile. Khandha: in the aggregates, beginning with form. Mūla: principal investment, capital. Upadā: a present, a gift. Dasā: in a state or condition, and at the fringe of a cloth. Ghāta: slaughter, killing.

1128. Gabbe [M 0.0595] māne. Ghaṭanaṃ silesakaraṇaṃ. Rāsi puñjo, etesu ghaṭasaddo. Abhihāre pūjāyaṃ. Bandhane “pākāracayo”tyādīsu.

1128. Gabbha: in the womb, in pride. Ghaṭana: joining, causing adhesion. Rāsi: a mass, a heap; in these senses is the word 'ghaṭa'. Abhihāra: in an offering, in reverence. Bandhana: in construction, as in “pākāracayo” (the building of a wall), and so on.

1129. Thoke appake. Dāne, hāniyañca cāgo. Gīvā, galo cāti dve abhidhānāni iṇe siyuṃ. “Iṇe gīvā galepi cā”tipi pāṭho. Gale kaṇṭhe.

1129. Thoka: in a little, in a small amount. Cāga: in giving, and in loss. Gīvā and galo—these two terms may be used for debt. “Iṇe gīvā galepi cā” (In debt, gīvā and also galo)—this is also a reading. Gala: in the throat, in the neck.

1130. Daṇḍepi sāhasaṃ. Paṭe vatthavisese bhaṅgaṃ. Sāṇādike missitvā katañhi vatthaṃ “bhaṅga”nti vuttaṃ. Chavake kaḷevare.

1130. Sāhasa: violence; also a penalty. Bhaṅga: in cloth, in a special kind of cloth. Indeed, cloth made by mixing hemp and the like is called “bhaṅga.” Chavaka: in a corpse, in a dead body.

1131. Anaṅge māre. Dume karahāṭake.

1131. Anaṅga: in the Bodiless One, in Māra. Duma: in a tree, in the karahāṭaka tree.

“Madano [M 0.0596] māradhuttara-vasantadumasitthake”ti vopālito. Pamātari mātumātari. Veṭhe uṇhīse ca veṭhanaṃ.

Thus Vopālita: "Madana is used for Māra, the dhuttara plant, the spring season, a tree, and beeswax." Pamātar: in a neglectful one; mātumātar: in a mother's mother. Veṭhana: in a wrapping, and in a turban.

1132. Taṇḍuleyye tilaphalasāke. Ayye sāmini. Mutti muccanaṃ.

1132. Taṇḍuleyya: in the sesame-fruit vegetable. Ayyā: in a lady, in a mistress. Mutti: release, liberation.

1133. Aṅke lakkhaṇe. Ākāre sīsacalanādike. Vappe vappanīyabīje. Taṭe tīre ca vappo, pākāramūle, nettajale, usume ca vappo. Anuññāyaṃ, vohāre ca sammutisaddo. Akkhatasaddo lājāsu dhaññavikatīsu napuṃsake.

1133. Aṅka: in the lap, in a mark. Ākāra: in a gesture, such as nodding the head and the like. Vappa: in a field, in seed to be sown. Vappo: on a bank, and on a shore; also at the base of a wall, in tears, and in heat. The word sammuti: in permission, and in conventional speech. The word akkhata: in parched grain, in grain products, in the neuter gender.

1134. Yāge devapūjāyaṃ, sadādāne ca satraṃ. Sasu hiṃsāyaṃ, traṇa, satraṃ. Osadhimhi, cande ca somo.

1134. Satra: in sacrifice, in worship of the gods, and in constant giving. Satra is derived from the root sasu, meaning violence, and tra, meaning protection. Somo: in a medicinal plant, and in the moon.

“Somo kuvere pitudevatāyaṃ,

Vasuppabhede vasudhākare ca;

Dibbosadhisāmalatāsamīra-

Kappūranīresu ca vānare cā”ti. –

“Soma is used for Kuvera, for the deity of the ancestors, for a type of Vasu, and for the moon; and for divine herbs, the sāma creeper, wind, camphor, water, and also for a monkey.”

Vopālito[M 0.0597]. Yugagehaṅgeti pubbāparāyāmavasena thambhānaṃ upari ṭhapite yugabhūte gehāvayave. Dakkhiṇuttarāyāmavasena ṭhapite gehaṅge saṅghāṭo.

According to Vopālita: 'Yugagehaṅga' is a house-part in the nature of a yoke, placed above the pillars along the front-to-back axis. 'Saṅghāṭa' is a house-part placed along the south-to-north axis.

Gāthāpādavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the feet of the verses is concluded.

Anekatthavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Anekatthavagga is concluded.

4. Abyayavaggavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Abyayavagga

1136-1137. Cirassādayo cattāro ciratthakā. Cirāya, cirā cātra. Sahādayopi cattāro sahatthā. Punappunamādayo pañca punappunatthā. Vinādayo pañca vajjanatthā.

1136-1137. The four terms beginning with 'cirassa' denote long duration. 'Cirāya' and 'cirā' are also included here. The four terms beginning with 'sahā' also denote association. The five terms beginning with 'punappunaṃ' denote repetition. The five terms beginning with 'vinā' denote exclusion.

1138. Balavaṃ [M 0.0598] suṭṭhu atīva kimuta su ati ete cha atisayatthe. Pasaṃsāyañca suṭṭhu. Pañhepi kimuta. Āho kiṃ kimu udāhu kimuta uda ete cha vikappe vitakke.
